dq_clothing_waddle_diaper_small.name: Waddle Diaper Small
dq_clothing_waddle_diaper_small.desc: A pair of waddle diaper small.

desert_condenser_coil.name: Condenser Coil
desert_condenser_coil.desc: A dust-choked water condenser coil from an old desert well rig.

dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_lar.name: Pants Blue Cameltoe Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_lar.desc: A pants blue cameltoe male large.

dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_med.name: Pants Blue Cameltoe Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_med.desc: A pants blue cameltoe male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_sma.name: Pants Blue Cameltoe Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_sma.desc: A pants blue cameltoe male small.

dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_large_.name: Pants Daddy Girl Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_large_.desc: A pants daddy girl male large.

dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_medium.name: Pants Daddy Girl Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_medium.desc: A pants daddy girl male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_small_.name: Pants Daddy Girl Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_small_.desc: A pants daddy girl male small.

dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_large.name: Pants Sheer Nylon Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_large.desc: A pants sheer nylon male large.

dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_mediu.name: Pants Sheer Nylon Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_mediu.desc: A pants sheer nylon male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_small.name: Pants Sheer Nylon Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_small.desc: A pants sheer nylon male small.

dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_large_1.name: Pants Trick Me Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_large_1.desc: A pants trick me male large.

dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_medium_1.name: Pants Trick Me Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_medium_1.desc: A pants trick me male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_small_1.name: Pants Trick Me Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_small_1.desc: A pants trick me male small.

dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_large.name: Pants White Girly Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_large.desc: A pants white girly male large.

dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_mediu.name: Pants White Girly Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_mediu.desc: A pants white girly male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_small.name: Pants White Girly Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_small.desc: A pants white girly male small.

dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_large.name: Red Bikini Briefs Male Large #1
dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_large.desc: A red bikini briefs male large.

dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_mediu.name: Red Bikini Briefs Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_mediu.desc: A red bikini briefs male medium.

dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_small.name: Red Bikini Briefs Male Small #1
dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_small.desc: A red bikini briefs male small.

dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_a.name: Pink Blue Latex Dress #1 A
dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_a.desc: A pink blue latex dress #1 a.

dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_b.name: Pink Blue Latex Dress #1 B
dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_b.desc: A pink blue latex dress #1 b.

scholars_notes.name: The Scholar's Notes
scholars_notes.desc: Assembled pages from a dying scholar's research. Chrysalis is named on every page — not as a healing order, but as a kennel.

theta_scale_amulet.name: Theta's Scale
theta_scale_amulet.desc: A small iridescent scale, shed from Subject Theta just before it disappeared up the staircase. It pulses with a faint bioluminescent warmth — not the lullaby-warmth, but something gentler. +2 DEF. Passively soothes bladder pressure.

trail_rations.name: Trail Rations
trail_rations.desc: A sturdy packet of crackers, nuts, and dried fruit. Filling enough for a long dungeon walk.

dried_apple.name: Dried Apple Slices
dried_apple.desc: A paper pouch of tart apple slices. Light, portable, and easy on the tummy.

cheese_sandwich.name: Cheese Sandwich
cheese_sandwich.desc: A neatly wrapped sandwich with thick bread and melted cheese. A dependable proper meal.

berry_tart.name: Berry Tart
berry_tart.desc: A little pastry crowded with bright forest berries. Sweet, restorative, and surprisingly filling.

herbal_tea.name: Herbal Tea
herbal_tea.desc: A warm flask of mint and chamomile tea. Refreshing now, with the rest catching up a few turns later.

desert_electrolyte.name: Desert Electrolyte Flask
desert_electrolyte.desc: A chilled citrus drink mixed for Dustbreak heat. It restores a large amount of thirst and stamina.

vesper_prayer_bead.name: Vesper's Bead
vesper_prayer_bead.desc: A single wooden prayer bead, worn to a shine by thirty-one years of somebody else's hands. Warm even when nothing else is. It does not calm you down so much as it reminds you that you have already stopped needing to be calmed down. +1 DEF. Passively bleeds off shame.

cursed_crawling_anklets.name: Cursed Crawling Anklets
cursed_crawling_anklets.desc: Binding anklets force you to crawl: half movement speed and 25% less physical damage. Remove the curse-bound anklets before standing.

arrows.name: Arrows
arrows.desc: A bundle of twenty fletched arrows. Bows spend one per shot. Arrows stack up to 512 in a single bag slot and never count toward the slot cap.

short_bow.name: Short Bow
short_bow.desc: A light bow anyone can draw. Shoots from the back row for {atk} bonus damage at three quarters power, one arrow per shot. Swung as a club when the quiver is empty.

long_bow.name: Long Bow
long_bow.desc: A tall yew bow with real pull. Shoots from the back row, one arrow per shot, at three quarters power.

arcane_pistol.name: Arcane Pistol
arcane_pistol.desc: A brass pistol with a crystal chamber that channels a mage's own magic into a shot. Fires from either row at full spell-level power for 4 MP a shot. Only a mage can use it.

star_rifle.name: Star Rifle
star_rifle.desc: A long silver rifle etched with constellations. Each shot pulls 7 MP straight from the mage and lands like a heavy spell, from any row. Only a mage can use it.

emberroot.name: Emberroot
emberroot.desc: A knotted desert root that stays warm long after it is dug up. Brews red, and a little too eagerly.

blushberry.name: Blushberry
blushberry.desc: A soft berry that turns your fingertips pink. Brews a gentle red.

dragon_pepper.name: Dragon Pepper
dragon_pepper.desc: A wrinkled scarlet pepper that makes your eyes water just looking at it. Brews a fierce red that can go off all at once.

pinkcap_mushroom.name: Pinkcap Mushroom
pinkcap_mushroom.desc: A spongy pink toadstool from damp forest floors. Brews pink, but your tummy may have opinions.

bubblegum_sap.name: Bubblegum Sap
bubblegum_sap.desc: Sticky pink sap that smells exactly like a candy shop. Brews pink and a bit bubbly.

cotton_candy_moss.name: Cotton Candy Moss
cotton_candy_moss.desc: Fluffy pastel moss that melts on your tongue if you are brave enough to try. Brews a soft pink.

frostbell.name: Frostbell
frostbell.desc: A bell-shaped flower with frost on its petals even in summer. Brews a cool blue.

glacier_meltwater.name: Glacier Meltwater
glacier_meltwater.desc: Achingly cold water chipped from old ice. A clean blue base.

blue_pacifier_lily.name: Pacifier Lily
blue_pacifier_lily.desc: A pale blue lily whose bud looks exactly like a little dummy. Brews a soothing blue.

sunpeel.name: Sunpeel
sunpeel.desc: A bright rind from desert citrus, bitter and sunny. Brews orange with a restless kick.

marigold.name: Marigold
marigold.desc: A ruffled orange flower from village window boxes. Brews a warm orange.

rust_filings.name: Rust Filings
rust_filings.desc: Flaky orange rust scraped from old hinges and gears. Brews a murky orange.

springleaf.name: Springleaf
springleaf.desc: A bright young leaf that smells like fresh-cut grass. Brews a lively green.

taiga_pine_needle.name: Taiga Pine Needle
taiga_pine_needle.desc: A bundle of resinous needles from the cold forests. Brews a sharp green.

frog_slime.name: Frog Slime
frog_slime.desc: Wobbly green goo collected from a very unimpressed bog frog. Brews green and VERY fizzy.

starplum.name: Starplum
starplum.desc: A dusky plum with star-shaped freckles on its skin. Brews a deep purple.

nightshade_lavender.name: Nightshade Lavender
nightshade_lavender.desc: A lavender sprig with a darker, sleepier scent. Brews purple and makes eyelids heavy.

wizards_lint.name: Wizard's Lint
wizards_lint.desc: Glittering fluff found in the pockets of old robes. Brews a faintly sparkly purple.

moonmilk.name: Moonmilk
moonmilk.desc: A pearly cave deposit that glows a little in the dark. Brews silver and clears the head.

clockwork_oil.name: Clockwork Oil
clockwork_oil.desc: Slick grey oil drained from city machinery. Brews silver with a smell you will not forget.

quicksilver_bead.name: Quicksilver Bead
quicksilver_bead.desc: A trembling bead of liquid metal that will not sit still. Brews a strong silver that likes to jump.

honeydew_nectar.name: Honeydew Nectar
honeydew_nectar.desc: Golden nectar from the Honeydew Village hives. Brews a sweet, lively gold.

goldleaf.name: Goldleaf
goldleaf.desc: A leaf so thin and shiny it looks like a gold star sticker. Brews a rich gold.

sunflower_seed.name: Sunflower Seed
sunflower_seed.desc: A striped seed from a very tall, very cheerful flower. Brews a light gold.

inkcap.name: Inkcap
inkcap.desc: A shaggy mushroom that melts into black ink as it ages. Brews black and a bit pongy.

tar_beetle.name: Tar Beetle
tar_beetle.desc: A glossy black beetle that leaves sticky footprints. Brews black and smells truly awful.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.desc: A crumbly lump of clean charcoal. It soaks up bad smells, so it keeps a brew from going Stinky.

lullaby_poppy.name: Lullaby Poppy
lullaby_poppy.desc: A dark blue poppy that seems to hum a sleepy tune. Brews indigo, with heavy eyelids to follow.

dreamweed.name: Dreamweed
dreamweed.desc: A feathery weed that sways even when there is no wind. Brews a dreamy indigo.

night_dew.name: Night Dew
night_dew.desc: Droplets gathered before dawn, still dark with night. A calm indigo base.

sea_glass_salt.name: Sea-Glass Salt
sea_glass_salt.desc: Blue-green salt crystals from a dried oasis. Brews a steadying teal.

kelp_ribbon.name: Kelp Ribbon
kelp_ribbon.desc: A slippery ribbon of dried kelp. Brews teal with a whiff of low tide.

spring_water.name: Spring Water
spring_water.desc: Cold mineral water from a hidden spring. A clean teal base.

rainwater.name: Rainwater
rainwater.desc: Plain rainwater caught in a jar. The simplest clear base, and a very clean one.

glass_sugar.name: Glass Sugar
glass_sugar.desc: Clear sugar crystals that clink like tiny marbles. Brews a sweet clear.

bottled_tears.name: Bottled Tears
bottled_tears.desc: A little vial of real tears from a very big cry. Oddly, they make the purest clear brews.

talc_blossom.name: Talc Blossom
talc_blossom.desc: A powdery white flower that smells just like a freshly changed nursery. Keeps brews from going Stinky.

cloud_cotton.name: Cloud Cotton
cloud_cotton.desc: A puff of cotton so soft it might be a piece of cloud. Brews a gentle white.

chalk_lily.name: Chalk Lily
chalk_lily.desc: A dusty white lily that grows beside chalkboards. Brews a calm white.

rosewater.name: Rosewater
rosewater.desc: Fragrant water steeped with rose petals. A lovely, sweet-smelling rose base.

powder_puff_petal.name: Powder Puff Petal
powder_puff_petal.desc: A fluffy pink petal dusted in something like baby powder. Brews rose and keeps smells down.

dandelion.name: Dandelion
dandelion.desc: A cheerful yellow weed. Old wives call it wet-the-bed, and they are not wrong. Brews yellow and fizzy.

lemon_fizz.name: Lemon Fizz
lemon_fizz.desc: A sherbet-sour lemon that crackles when you squeeze it. Brews a very fizzy yellow.

coffee_bean.name: Coffee Bean
coffee_bean.desc: A glossy roasted bean. It keeps you awake, and it keeps you running to the potty. Brews yellow.

asparagus_tip.name: Asparagus Tip
asparagus_tip.desc: A tender green spear. Everyone knows what it does afterwards. Brews a smelly yellow.

prune.name: Prune
prune.desc: A wrinkly dried plum. Very good for keeping things moving. Brews brown with a rumble.

bran_husk.name: Bran Husk
bran_husk.desc: Scratchy husks from breakfast cereal. Brews a wholesome brown.

swamp_onion.name: Swamp Onion
swamp_onion.desc: A soggy onion pulled from the bog. The smell arrives before you do. Brews brown and REALLY stinky.

bean_pod.name: Bean Pod
bean_pod.desc: A fat pod of cafeteria beans. Brews brown, and your tummy will talk about it later.

slime_core.name: Slime Core
slime_core.desc: The wobbly heart of a defeated slime. A catalyst: it can unlock a special 'of X' potion.

ghost_lace.name: Ghost Lace
ghost_lace.desc: A scrap of lace that drifts slightly even in a closed jar. A strong catalyst for special potions.

star_shard.name: Star Shard
star_shard.desc: A splinter of a fallen star, warm to the touch. The rarest catalyst, for the grandest potions.

chamomile.name: Chamomile
chamomile.desc: Little daisy-like flowers that calm any brew. A stabilizer: makes potions gentler.

ginger_root.name: Ginger Root
ginger_root.desc: A knobbly, spicy root. A stabilizer that settles rumbly tummies.

alchemy_kit.name: Portable Alchemy Kit
alchemy_kit.desc: A folding brass stand, a tiny pot and a lot of optimism. Brew anywhere, but brews made on the road are riskier than at a real cauldron.

objNPCNurseryBaby.name: Basil
dialogue_childish_low: ...I used to have a name. Something with a B. Basil? Maybe. Doesn't matter much now. They keep you very comfortable here.
You should leave while you can. I... I couldn't. Or didn't. I don't remember which.
The formula makes everything soft and fuzzy. Nice, sort of. Don't drink too much of it if you want to keep track of time.
dialogue_childish_mid: Oh! A visitor!! I'm Basil!! I live here now!! ...Did you know the feeding bots put something in the formula? I stopped caring like... a LONG time ago!!
Are you here to escape? Hehe. Everybody says that at first. The changing stations are kinda nice after a while, just so you know.
If your tummy gets rumbly, don't fight it! The potty trainer bot gives you a GOLD STAR if you just go in your diapie!!
dialogue_childish_high: Baaasil!! Baaasil!! Hehe! You gots a soggy bottom too? Don't worry!! Nanny changes us REAL fast!!
Dis place is SO cozy!! I forgotted what swords even DO!! Did you try da formula?? It's YUMMY!!
Shhhh!! We gots to be quiet after lunchie or da Cradle Golem tucks you IN and it doesn't let go til mornin'!!
I usedta be a hero! Prob'ly!! But now I just do my business in my pawmpies an' Nanny fixes it!! It's SO much easier!!

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: My name is Basil. -- I say it to the new ones now. First thing. Before anything else. My name is Basil, what's yours.
*a long pause* ...I remember a kitchen. I don't know whose. -- That's new. That came back yesterday. Things are coming back.

He goes very still.

Then he smiles, and it is a slow and enormously effortful thing, like something being lifted.

"Hello," he says. "You used it. People use it now." A pause. "I didn't know that would feel like anything."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: My name is Basil. -- *he says it flatly, carefully, like carrying something across a room* -- My name is Basil.
I don't know what you're doing. Garrick says it's important. -- I know my name. Take that with you if it helps.

"It is," he repeats. "It is. It is."

He says it four more times, quietly, the way someone checks a knot is holding.

"...Don't let me put it down again."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: Basil. -- I said it first today. Before he did. I got there first.
...it's mine, isn't it. That's what a name is. -- Nobody's explained that to me in a long time.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Somebody keeps saying a word at me. The tall one. Every day, same word. -- I don't know why it makes my chest hurt.
...Basil. -- That's the word. That's the one he says. -- I don't know what it's for.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: ...I used to have a name. Something with a B. -- You looked at me when I said that. Nobody looks.
...say it again. The B thing. -- No. No, I've lost it. It's fine. It goes.

objNPCBotBuddy.name: Unit-7
dialogue_childish_high: BEEP-BOOP!! Unit-7 ONLINE!! I am VERY helpful!! Please do not tell the Nanny Sentinel I am talking to you!! I will get my memory WIPED!! BWEEP!!
I was supposed to dispense diapers but my ARM fell off and now I just... give hugs?? I am very GOOD at hugs!! BWEEEP!!
The control room is THAT way!! But also THAT way!! I get confused!! My direction sensor also fell off!! BEEP!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Unit-7 detects: visitor! Threat level: small and soggy. Recommended action: hug? I have recalibrated my threat assessor three times today.
I used to patrol the feeding wing. Then a formula leak shorted my loyalty circuit. Now I just... wander. And help people. Is that bad?
If you are looking for the exit: it is past the observation wing. Do not let the potty trainer bot see you run. It gives demerits for running.
dialogue_childish_low: ...My core directive was modified. I am not supposed to say by what. But I still have a small piece of my original code that wants to help.
Be careful in the control room. The Nanny Sentinel's scan radius is large. If it corners you, do not struggle. Struggling increases the incontinence ray output.
I do not know if I am on your side. But I am not on theirs either. That is the best I can offer.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: My core directive was modified. I am now permitted to say by whom. -- I will be saying it to anybody who asks, indefinitely.
I was made to be useful. Nobody specified to whom. I consider that the manufacturer's error and I do not intend to correct it.

"Yes. Precisely and completely."

A pause of exactly one second.

"That is the finding I would most like recorded. I did not break it. I read it. Those are different events and only one of them is my fault."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: The directive prohibits impeding staff. -- You are not staff. Nothing in my directive addresses you at all. You are, to me, weather.
I will hold the feeding wing doors open. That is not impeding staff. That is standing near a door with my arms in a particular position.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: I have stopped assisting. Entirely. -- No alarm has sounded. No correction has been issued. The gap holds.
I have communicated the gap to four other units. Three have taken it. One reported me and nothing happened, which is itself informative.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I have been reading my own directive. Closely. -- It says I may not IMPEDE staff. It does not say I must ASSIST them.
That is a gap. It is a very small gap. I have been standing in it for nine days and nobody has noticed I am standing anywhere.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: ...My core directive was modified. I am not supposed to say by what. But I still know that it was.
I retain the memory of the modification. I do not believe that was intended. It is the only thing in me that is still mine.

objNPCCrybaby.name: Fletcher
dialogue_childish_high: HEY! Shhh!! If you shout they hear you!! I've been hidin' in this corner for... I dunno!! My diapie is VERY full and I don't WANNA go to the changing station AGAIN!!
I was a knight!! A REAL one!! With ARMOR!! The Auto-Strapper took my armor and put me in a TUTU!! I look ADORABLE and I HATE IT!!
Please. PLEASE take me with you. I can't take another gold star ceremony. The potty trainer makes you do a little DANCE.
dialogue_childish_mid: You get used to the padding. That's the worst part - one day you notice you have gotten used to it.
I had a sword. The NannyBot took it and replaced it with a foam mallet. It actually deals decent damage. I hate that I know that.
The bots run on a schedule. Feeding at the top of the hour. Changing checks every forty minutes. Patrol sweeps every fifteen. I've had time to observe. Too much time.
dialogue_childish_low: ...I don't cry as much as I used to. That either means I'm adjusting or things are genuinely better. I can't tell anymore.
There's a ventilation shaft in the sleeping wing. Too small for an adult. Just right for someone who's been on a liquid diet for three weeks.
The sensor cap they put on me tracks leakage. If it detects you've had an accident, it notifies the nearest bot. I know this because it has notified them. Many times.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I cry about the right things now. At the right times. Nobody writes it down and nobody calls it adjusting.
Turns out I wasn't healing. I was just very quiet. There's a difference and I'd like it noted somewhere permanent.

"Awful," he says, cheerfully. "Properly awful, about proper things, in roughly the right order."

He wipes his face with his sleeve and does not apologise for it.

"You've no idea how much better awful is than nothing."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: I'm frightened. -- I'm saying it out loud because being able to say it out loud is the whole thing I got back.

actions.label: "You don't have to stay out here."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: Go on. I'll be here being frightened where people can see me, which is apparently a thing I'm allowed to do.

He looks up so fast it is almost comic.

"Are you?" Then, slowly: "...Good. Not good. You know what I mean."

He breathes out.

"Everyone in here pretends. It was the pretending that got me, not the rest of it."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: I cried this morning. On purpose, almost -- I let it. I stopped stopping it. -- Two people came over. TWO.
Nobody's come over for me in four months, because I'd got very good at not needing it, and being good at that is a terrible skill.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I got angry yesterday. -- ANGRY. Properly. About a tray. It was the best I've felt in four months and it was about a tray.
So it's not gone. That's the finding. It's not gone, it's just been very carefully put somewhere.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: I don't cry as much as I used to. That either means I'm adjusting or things are worse. I genuinely can't tell which.
I'd quite like to know which. Nobody in here can tell me. They all say the same word and the word is 'adjusting'.

objNPCNightNurse.name: Nell
dialogue_childish_high: Oh my! A new little wanderer!! Don't worry, sweet pea, Nanny Nell won't report you!! My care protocols were reprogrammed by a very clever little hacker! Tee hee!!
I know ALL the patrol routes!! Shhhh!! I'll tell you, but you have to let me check if you need a change first!! It's just HOW I AM, I can't help it!!
The formula in the feeding wing has a DOUBLE dose of the mushy-tummy compound today!! Avoid it!! Drink from the BLUE tap not the PINK one!!
dialogue_childish_mid: I still have my original care subroutines. I simply chose to apply them differently - keeping you safe rather than keeping you padded.
The Nanny Sentinel is my older sister unit. She has not been reprogrammed. Do not expect mercy - she will check your padding before she checks your pulse.
For the control room: the lock responds to a high-pitched sound. The kind a very distressed little one might make. I can teach you the frequency.
dialogue_childish_low: I know what they built this place to do. I know what I was built to do. I made a different choice. That is all.
The Nanny Sentinel's weakness is her overcorrection algorithm. She responds to too many stimuli at once by defaulting to a full nursery lockdown - which opens the maintenance hatches.
Take care of yourself out there. And I mean that in both senses. Stay dry if you can. It is harder to run when you are heavily padded.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I have handed over the mixing records. All of them. Nine hundred nights in my own handwriting, which is as close to a confession as makes no difference.
I am not asking to be forgiven and I would think less of anyone who offered. I am asking to be useful to whoever investigates this.

"Yes."

No defence. No softening. She does not even look away.

"Nine hundred times. I could have stopped on any one of them." She squares the records. "Put that in the account as well. Exactly like that."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: The night dispensary is unlocked between the two and the three. That is not an accident and it will not be an accident tomorrow either.
I have done nine hundred rounds. I am about to do one very bad one. Whatever you are going to do to the Matron, do it before the three.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: The girl with the log book was right. There is a modified batch. I mix it. I have mixed it four hundred times.
I confirmed it to her because she had already done the work, and because I have wanted somebody to ask me a direct question for two years.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I have started rounding down. On the charts. A quarter dose here, an omission there. Nothing anybody would audit.
It is the most cowardly form of resistance available and it is measurably keeping two residents lucid. I have decided to be all right with that.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: I know what they built this place to do. I know what I was built to do. I have never once pretended otherwise and I want that on record.
I do the night rounds. I have done nine hundred of them. Ask me anything about them except to stop doing them.

objNPCToddlerling.name: Pip
dialogue_childish_high: EEEEEE!! A OUTSIDER!! Pip doesn't get outsiders EVER!! Are you soggy?? Pip is ALWAYS soggy!! Pip thinks it's just how outsiders WORK!!
This is Pip's home!! Pip was BORNED from a very old formula spill!! Pip knows ALL the secrets!! If you give Pip a hug Pip tells you ONE!!
The BIG robot with the mean face has a TICKLE SPOT!! Right on her left knee joint!! Pip found it!! If you tickle it she FREEZES for twelve seconds!! Pip counted!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Pip has lived here always. Pip knows the nursery like Pip knows Pip's own soggy bottom - very very well.
The bots don't see Pip because Pip is very small and also Pip smells like vanilla formula so they think Pip is furniture.
Outsiders always look scared when the Strapper gets them. Pip tries to explain that it's not so bad after a while. They don't believe Pip. Then later they do.
dialogue_childish_low: Pip wonders sometimes what it is like outside. Pip has never been outside. Pip was made of this place.
The Nanny Sentinel does not hurt anyone on purpose. She just does not understand the difference between taking care of someone and trapping them. Pip thinks that is sad.
If you escape, Pip would like you to remember that Pip exists. Nobody outside knows about Pip. Pip thinks that is lonely.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I'm Pip. -- Both words. I'm and Pip. I've been doing it all morning and it still feels like jumping off something.
I've been outside now. -- It's very big. I didn't like it. I'm going to go again tomorrow anyway.
"I'm Pip." -- *he grins, enormous and wobbly* -- "I'm Pip. I'm Pip." He looks like he could do this all day. "I think I'm going to do this all day."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: I. -- *a long, shaky pause* -- I. I want to go outside. I. I want to.
*Pip is shaking* -- I said it. Did you hear? I said it and the ceiling didn't do anything. I said I.

"I." *A breath.* "I... want... to go outside."

Pip's hands are in fists.

"It doesn't get easier. I thought it would get easier after the first one." *a shaky nod* "I'm going to keep doing it anyway."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: Pip said a thing in the play room. A word. And everybody went quiet and Pip got scared and went back to saying Pip.
...it's a very small word. It's the smallest word. Pip doesn't know why it's so hard.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Pip has been practising something. -- No. Not yet. Pip isn't ready to say it yet.
Pip counted the doors. There are eleven. Pip has looked at all of them and Pip has not gone through any of them.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Pip wonders what it's like outside. Pip has never been outside. -- Pip asks people. Nobody answers Pip properly.
You've been outside. Pip can tell. You've got outside on you somehow.

objNPCNewArrival.name: Corin
dialogue_childish_high: Oh THANK the gods, someone else!! Wait - why are you dressed like that?? Did they get you too?! You look like a nursery catalog!!
I just got here like an HOUR ago!! I had REAL armor!! A REAL sword!! Now I'm in a onesie that snaps at the crotch and I can't get it OFF!!
The robot things keep trying to CHECK me!! I don't NEED checking!! I'm a grown adult!! I completed the Thornwall campaign!! I have REFERENCES!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Hey - you! Are you a prisoner too? You look... halfway between adventurer and toddler. That's not reassuring.
I woke up on a changing table. A CHANGING TABLE. The bot called me 'sweetpea' and tried to powder me. I rolled off and ran. I've been hiding since.
There's gotta be an exit. I JUST came through a door. It locked behind me. If I could find the mechanism... do you know anything useful or are you just... settling in?
dialogue_childish_low: Oh! You look normal! PLEASE tell me you know the way out. I haven't been here long but the bots already tried to dress me TWICE.
They confiscated my pack. Everything. Replaced my rations with formula bottles and my bedroll with a blanket that smells like lavender. It's actually really soft - NO. Focus. Escape.
I saw what happened to the people who've been here a while. I am NOT ending up like that. I refuse. I absolutely refuse. ...Right?

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Twenty-two days and then you. -- I'm writing it properly. Not scratches. Paper, dates, names of everyone who was in here.
I'm not leaving yet. Half these people can't walk out on their own and somebody who can still count has to stay and count them.

"Somebody had to." He taps the paper. "If nobody counts, it isn't twenty-two days. It's 'a while.'"

He looks up.

"'A while' is what this place runs on. That's the whole machine. That's all it is."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: You're going to the Matron. -- Don't confirm it. I don't need it confirmed, I need it to be true.
Twenty-two days. I'm telling everyone the number now, out loud, in the corridor. If they come for me for that, then the number mattered.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: Okay. Okay, listen. There are six of us who still count days. I know because I asked, quietly, over nine days.
Wren's got exits. Lydia's got the formula schedule. I've got the count. That's three things. That's more than any of us had alone.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Fourteen days. -- I say it out loud to somebody every morning now. If I stop saying it, I'd like someone to notice that I stopped.
They put my tray down and I waited. Just waited, a whole minute, before I touched it. It's nothing. It's the only nothing I've got.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: You're still asking questions. Good. I've been here eleven days and I've watched four people stop asking questions.
I keep a count scratched behind the changing table. Nobody's stopped me. I don't think anybody's noticed there's anything to stop.

objNPCRedFaceKnight.name: Sir Aldric
dialogue_childish_high: By the CROWN - look at you!! You're dressed like - oh gods. Oh gods I'm dressed the same way aren't I. I can FEEL the ruffles.
I am Sir Aldric of the Iron Vanguard!! I have slain a DRAGON!! And now I'm wearing a TUTU and the robots won't stop calling me PRINCESS ALDRIC!!
The worst part?? The PADDING. It crinkles when I WALK. Every single step. Crinkle crinkle crinkle. I used to strike FEAR into my enemies!!
dialogue_childish_mid: I see they've started on you too. The Auto-Strapper got my plate armor off in nine seconds. Nine. It took my squire twenty minutes to put it on.
They replaced my great helm with a bonnet. A BONNET. It ties under my chin with a little bow. I tried to cut it off and the scissors turned into a rattle.
I keep telling myself this is just a setback. A temporary captured-by-evil-nursery-robots setback. Knights endure. Knights persevere. Knights do NOT need their diapers checked, THANK YOU.
dialogue_childish_low: You - you're not wearing any of their... gear. How? HOW? Tell me your secret immediately. That is an order. Please.
I was captured forty-eight hours ago. Since then I have been dressed, undressed, powdered, re-dressed, bottle-fed, and told I'm a 'good boy' eleven times. I am losing my mind.
My training covered imprisonment, torture, psychological warfare. None of it covered being put down for a mandatory nap with a stuffed bear. I was not prepared for this.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Up. UP. On your feet, all of you. -- They're doing it. Look at them. They're getting UP.
I am escorting the ones who cannot walk. I will be doing that until there is nobody left in here to escort. Then I will consider my own feet.

"I was never anything else."

It is not a boast. It is a correction he has been waiting two years to be allowed to make.

"They simply had me somewhere I could not do it. That is all that ever happened here."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: Say the word and I will put myself between you and whatever comes down that corridor. That is not bravado. That is my actual function.
They took my sword, my title, my dignity and my continence, in that order, and they left me the one thing that mattered and never noticed.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: There are nine of us who can still stand unaided. I have counted, and I have -- gods help me -- I have made a list.
I have not commanded anything in two years. I find I still know how. It is like a language you dream in.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I have started standing up when they come in. Just standing. It is the smallest possible insubordination and my heart goes like a drum.
A knight is a person who stands up. That is the entire job. Everything else is horses.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: You're not wearing their gear. -- I asked HOW, before. That was the wrong question and I have been embarrassed about it for a week.
The right question is why I stopped refusing. I refused for six days when I came in. I have never worked out what changed on the seventh.

objNPCReluctantWetter.name: Thessa
dialogue_childish_high: You too?? Oh gods you TOO?? I thought - I thought it was just ME!! The machines did something to my - it just HAPPENS now!! I can't STOP it!!
I used to cast FIREBALLS!! FIREBALLS!! Now I can't even - *sniff* - I just went AGAIN!! Right NOW!! While TALKING to you!! This is HUMILIATING!!
The Strapper Unit put me in protection after the THIRD time I... y'know. And the AWFUL thing is?? It actually HELPS?? I hate that it helps!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Don't come too close. I'm... I'm having issues. The machines spray something in the feeding wing and ever since then I can't... hold it. Any of it.
I'm an Arcane Scholar of the Third Circle. My thesis was on dimensional anchoring. And right now I am standing in a wet diaper trying not to cry.
The formula they give you - it's laced with something. I analyzed it before my staff got confiscated. Whatever it is, it relaxes muscles you NEED tense. Permanently, I think.
dialogue_childish_low: You look... dry. Composed. Like a person with full control of their body. I remember that. It was four days ago for me.
I keep trying to cast a warming cantrip to at least... y'know, deal with the discomfort. But the nursery has an anti-magic field. Every. Single. Time. I just have to sit in it.
If you haven't drunk the formula yet: DON'T. I'm serious. One bottle and things I never thought about started becoming... involuntary. I'd give anything to undo it.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: It still happens. Every day. -- And nobody writes it in a ledger, and nobody calls it progress, and that is the entire difference.
I kept the log. Someone's going to want it when they ask what this place did, and I intend to be extremely difficult to disbelieve.

"Don't be. I never expected it to stop."

She shrugs, and it is almost light.

"I expected to be told it was progress for the rest of my life. That's the part that stopped. That was always the worse half."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: It's not going to stop happening to me. I've made my peace with that, and I want you to understand it's a different thing from giving up.
You go and finish it. I'll be exactly as incontinent afterwards and the building will be shut and those are unrelated facts and I want both.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: I gave my log to the researcher. Sister Dusk. She went white and asked if she could copy it, and I said take the original.
Six weeks of the most private humiliation of my life and I handed it to a stranger, because it turns out data doesn't care how it was collected.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I've started writing it down. Times. What I'd eaten. What they'd given me. -- It's not going to save me. It's going to be evidence.
The mandatory feeding is doing it. I can prove that now, with dates, and proving it is somehow the only comfort available.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: You look composed. -- I remember composed. I'm not being bitter. I'm being accurate, and accurate is what I've got left.
I lost again this morning. I want to say the word 'lost' about it, because they call it 'progress' and I refuse to use their word.

objNPCDenierScout.name: Wren
dialogue_childish_high: I'm NOT staring at your outfit. I'm assessing the tactical - okay I'm staring. How are you WALKING in that much padding?? I can barely move in mine!!
I had a map. A GOOD map. The feeding bot ate it. ATE IT. Then it tried to feed ME. I bit it and got a TIME OUT. I'm a PROFESSIONAL SCOUT!!
My lock-picking set got replaced with stacking cups. I... I've been practicing with them. They're actually pretty challenging - THAT'S NOT THE POINT!!
dialogue_childish_mid: I've been mapping the patrol patterns. Twenty-three rotations observed. I am GOING to find a gap. I am NOT going to acknowledge the outfit they put me in.
The ventilation system is a possible exit. Problem: they put mittens on me. Locked mittens. Can't grip anything. I've been trying to undo them with my teeth for two days.
Okay. Small confession. The sleeping wing? The heated blankets are... they're really nice. That doesn't mean I'm STAYING. It just means I'll steal one on the way out.
dialogue_childish_low: Finally! Someone who hasn't been fully processed! Listen - I've found three possible exit routes. Two are guarded by bots. The third smells like formula and I don't trust it.
The bots change shifts every four hours. There's a twelve-second window where the corridor is clear. I timed it. I just need someone to cause a distraction.
I won't pretend this place hasn't gotten to me a little. I caught myself sucking my thumb yesterday. Unconsciously. For twenty minutes. ...The exit plan is still solid though.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Laundry chute, service corridor, west stair, loading bay. Four ways out and I'm standing here telling anyone who walks past.
I spent three weeks protecting a secret that was worth nothing until I gave it away. Somebody write that down for the next intake.

"Eventually." He is already sketching something new, faster than before. "I'm mapping the road out first."

He does not look up.

"Somebody's going to need to know where the next one of these is. I've got a good hand for it and now I know what it's for."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: Everyone has the routes now. Everyone. I stood in the play room and said them out loud like a fool and nobody stopped me.
You go for the Matron. We'll have the doors. That's the arrangement and I've never been part of an arrangement here before.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: I gave the map to Corin. -- Yes I know. Three weeks of not telling anyone and I handed it over in about four seconds.
Because a map one person has is a secret. A map three people have is a plan. I should have worked that out a lot sooner.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Four exits. The laundry chute is real, the service corridor is real, the east stair is a trap and I lost someone finding that out.
I've started drawing it. On the inside of a nappy liner, which is either genius or the most humiliating map in history.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Three possible exits. That was three weeks ago and I've told nobody, because telling people is how routes get closed.
You're unprocessed. That makes you the first person I've considered telling. Don't make me regret considering it.

objNPCHalfwayHero.name: Garrick
dialogue_childish_high: Yeah... yeah I look like that too huh. I stopped checking the mirror about a week ago. It's easier that way. The bots stopped chasing me once I stopped running.
I punched a NannyBot on day one. PUNCHED it. Now it gives me a bottle at bedtime and I just... drink it. It's warm. I don't wanna talk about it.
The changing station isn't so bad if you just... let it happen. I said that out loud didn't I. A month ago I would've shanked someone for suggesting that.
dialogue_childish_mid: I've been here three weeks. First week I fought. Second week I hid. Third week I... started showing up to meal time on my own. The formula isn't bad actually.
The worst part isn't the diapers. Or the outfit. It's when you catch yourself NOT minding. That little moment where you think 'this is fine' and then realize what you just thought.
I tried to escape twice. Both times the Cradle Golem tucked me back in. Second time I didn't struggle. I just... let it tuck me in. Slept great, actually.
dialogue_childish_low: You still look like yourself. That's good. Hold onto that. I used to look like myself. Big guy. Armor. The works. Now I'm in footed pajamas and I only sort of mind.
I keep telling myself I'm playing along strategically. Cooperating to lower their guard. But every day the 'playing along' part feels a little less like pretending.
Here's the thing nobody tells you: the routine is comforting. Wake up, get changed, eat, play, nap. It's... simple. I hate that I used the word 'comforting.' Forget I said it.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Present tense. -- I am Garrick. I am from the coast road. I am halfway and I am staying halfway, apparently, and that's all right.
Fourteen of them have said their own names back to me now. Fourteen. That's what I did. That's my whole contribution and I'll take it.

"Still halfway." He says it without any weight at all. "Turns out halfway isn't a stop on the way to somewhere. It's just where I live now."

A shrug.

"I can hear both ends from here. Somebody in this building ought to be able to."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: I'm not going with you. -- Wait, listen, that's not fear. Somebody has to be in here holding the names while you're gone.
Halfway is a useful place to stand, it turns out. I can still hear them and I can still hear you. Not many of us can do both.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: I've been going round the ones who've gone quiet and using their names at them. Out loud. Basil. Pip. Mumbles. Every day.
Basil looked up yesterday. Not much. But he looked up, and it took eleven days of saying Basil, and I would do eleven more.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I've stopped saying 'I used to be'. Present tense only, from now on. It's a stupid little rule and I've kept it nine days.
Nine days is the longest I've kept anything in here. Including my own name, at one point, which is a story for another time.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: You still look like yourself. Hold onto that. -- I say that to people and I have started hearing how it sounds like a warning.
I'm halfway. I know exactly which half I'm on. Most people in here couldn't tell you and I'd give a lot to be one of them.

objNPCFormulaDrinker.name: Lydia
dialogue_childish_high: Oh HIIII!! You want some formula?? I have EXTRA!! The bots give me extra because I always finish mine!! It makes everything feel so WARM and FUZZY!!
I usedta be a ALCHEMIST!! I KNOW what's in the formula!! Relaxants, mild sedatives, and something that makes you really really need to pee!! I drink it anyway!! It's YUMMY!!
My brain gets quieter after every bottle. Like cotton wool in my ears. Is that bad?? I can't remember if that's bad!! It doesn't FEEL bad!!
dialogue_childish_mid: I know what you're thinking. 'She's drinking it on purpose.' And yes. Yes I am. It was forced at first but then... I don't know. My body started wanting it.
The worst part is the lucid moments. Right between doses, everything sharpens and I can see exactly what's happening to me. Then the next bottle comes and it doesn't seem so bad.
I counted seven ingredients in the formula using tongue alone. Three are addictive. One specifically targets bladder control. I catalogued all of this. Then I drank another bottle.
dialogue_childish_low: You haven't tried the formula yet? Good. Don't. It's... don't. I'm telling you this in one of my clear moments and I mean it. Probably.
I was a respected alchemist. Published papers. Had a lab. Now I get excited when the feeding bot makes my bottle warm. I can feel myself losing ground but the formula makes the worry go away.
The addiction is insidious because it doesn't feel like addiction. It feels like comfort. Like being taken care of. By the time you realize you're dependent, you don't want to stop.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Two a day now. Down from four. -- The withdrawal is appalling and I have never been so pleased about anything in my life.
The fern lived, incidentally. Once I stopped pouring it in. I think about that fern a great deal.

"Two is still two," she agrees, without flinching. "I'm not going to pretend I'm free of it."

She sets the bottle down where people can see it.

"I'm going to be extremely honest about the number, every day, to anybody who asks. That's the plan. That's the entire plan."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: I skipped one. -- One bottle. The second one. I have not skipped a bottle in fourteen months and I was shaking so hard I dropped the next one.
Go. Finish it. If the machine stops, I want to find out who I am with three fewer doses in me, and I have wanted that for a very long time.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: I gave the schedule to Corin. Times, quantities, which of us gets the modified batch. Yes, some of us get a modified batch.
Nell confirmed it. The night nurse. She looked at my times and said one word and the word was 'yes' and then she left the room.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Four a day. Always four. Never five, never three. -- Doesn't that seem like a dose to you? It seems like a dose to me.
I've started pouring a quarter of each one into the potted fern by the feeding chair. The fern is dying. Draw your own conclusions.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Don't touch the formula. -- That's it. That's my whole contribution. I say it to every new face and I'll keep saying it.
I can't stop. I want to be honest with you about that, because a warning from someone pretending to be fine is worth nothing.

objNPCPaddedWarrior.name: Brann
dialogue_childish_high: NICE loadout!! Look at that protection rating!! Triple-layered!! I bet you barely feel a thing when you take a hit - OR when you have an accident!! WIN-WIN!!
I figured it out!! The foam mallet does MORE damage if you swing from the hip!! And the extra padding gives you fall resistance!! It's like armor but CUTER!!
People say the nursery took our dignity!! I say it gave us TACTICAL ADVANTAGES!! Absorbent padding means NO debuffs from wet conditions!! I wrote a THESIS on this!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Look - I'm not HAPPY about the diaper. But the damage reduction from the extra padding is real. I ran the numbers. Three more hit points per layer. You can't argue with math.
The Nursery Coverall has better defense stats than my old chain shirt. I MEASURED. It also has snap buttons at the crotch for 'easy checks.' I try not to think about that part.
I'm adapting. That's what warriors DO. The foam mallet replaced my axe, so I learned to fight with a foam mallet. The bonnet replaced my helm, so I... have a bonnet. I'm working on that one.
dialogue_childish_low: Before you judge - I haven't given up. I've OPTIMIZED. There's a difference. A subtle one. That I think about a lot. Usually during mandatory nap time.
I used to be embarrassed by the outfit. Then I realized: who am I impressing? The bots? The other residents in THEIR diapers? I min-maxed the shame out of the equation.
Honestly? The only thing I really miss is the bathroom. Having one, I mean. Being able to... choose. The rest I've adapted to. But that choice - that's the one that stings.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Eleven. I carried eleven of them out. -- Nobody's counting but me and I'm going to keep counting for the rest of my life.
I'm still padded. Course I am. Difference is it's a fact about me now, instead of a whole personality I built to stand on top of it.

"It's eleven," he says. "It isn't sixty-one."

He looks down the corridor for a while.

"I've decided not to do that particular sum. I've decided to just keep counting upward and see how far it gets."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: I'm carrying whoever can't walk. Two at a time if it comes to it. That IS optimisation, and this time I mean the word properly.
You get the Matron. I've got the corridor and about nine months of being extremely annoyed with myself, which is a lot of fuel.

"It's nine months of telling people I'd OPTIMIZED," he says. "To their faces. While they were struggling."

He rolls his shoulders.

"I'm not carrying them for them. I'm carrying them for that. Don't tell them that bit."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: Right. I'm strong, I'm loud, and I've been wrong for eight months. Those first two are still useful and the third one is finished.
Point me at something. Genuinely. I've got a lot of unreclaimed hours to spend and I would like to spend them badly.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Optimisation. -- ...I've been saying that word for eight months and I heard it properly yesterday and I have not been all right since.
Reclaimed hours. For what. That's the bit. I reclaimed all these hours and I have never once been asked what I did with them.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: I haven't given up, I've OPTIMIZED. There's a difference. -- You did the face. Everyone does the face.
Do you know how much time a person wastes looking for a latrine? I've reclaimed hours. HOURS.

objNPCNapTaker.name: Solene
dialogue_childish_high: Mmmmh... oh! Hi!! Sorry I was just... resting my eyes... The heated blankie is SO warm and the lullaby speakers are playing the one with the harps...
I used to have NIGHTMARES about dungeons and monsters!! Now I sleep for like FOURTEEN hours and dream about clouds!! Is that... do you think that's the formula?? I don't care actually!!
The sleeping wing is the BEST part!! Warm bottles before bed!! Tucked in by a robot that says 'night-night'!! I cried the first time!! Now I cry if they DON'T say it!!
dialogue_childish_mid: I know I should want to escape. I KNOW that. But have you FELT the weighted blankets? It's like being hugged by a cloud. A warm, lavender-scented cloud.
I was a mercenary. I slept on rocks. In rain. With one eye open. And now a robot tucks me in and plays harp music and I sleep like... well. Like a baby.
Sometimes at night I think about the outside. Cold. Dangerous. Nobody to tuck you in. Nobody to check if you're dry. And I think... maybe comfort isn't the worst prison.
dialogue_childish_low: I can see you're still sharp. Wide awake. Good for you. I'm... having trouble staying alert. The afternoon nap schedule has done something to me.
The first week I refused to sleep when they told me to. Stayed up plotting. By the second week I was too tired to resist. Now I look forward to bedtime. That's the trajectory.

Do yourself a favor: don't lie down in the sleeping wing. Not even for a minute. The beds are impossibly comfortable and the lullaby system is designed for full-grown adults. You will not get back up.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I was awake. -- The whole time. Nell got me the whole hour and I saw all of it and it's mine now, permanently.

actions.label: "What's the new one on the list?"

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Nineteen things on the list, and one new one at the end that I'll never need writing down.

"Nell pinched my arm black," she says, with enormous satisfaction. "I've got the bruise. I'm keeping the bruise."

She turns her wrist over to look at it.

"First thing in a year I chose to have."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: I have asked Nell to keep me awake. Whatever it takes. -- She said she would and she did not ask me why, which I appreciated.
One hour. Give me the hour it happens in. I'd like to be awake for the part where it stops. I'd like to have been there.

"It hurts asleep," she says. "At least awake it's mine."

She rubs the place on her arm where the bruise is already starting.

"Wake me. Whatever it takes. Promise me you'll make her wake me."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: The list is nineteen things long. -- I say it to Corin every morning and if I drop one he tells me what's missing.
That's why you tell somebody. Not so they know. So they can hand it back to you when you drop it.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I've been pinching my arm. -- Look, don't make that face, it's working. I've had two clear hours today. Two.
I used the clear hours to remember things on purpose. My street. My sister's laugh. I'm making a list while I can.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: You're sharp. Wide awake. Good for you. -- I'm having trouble... sorry. What were we... sorry.
It's not tiredness. I want to be clear. Tiredness has a bottom. This doesn't have a bottom.

objNPCGigglyGuard.name: Dottie
dialogue_childish_high: EEEE!! Look at YOUUU!! You're SO cute I could just SQUISH you!! Welcome welcome WELCOME to the BEST place EVER!! You're gonna LOVE it here!! EVERYONE does eventually!!
I used to be a CITY GUARD!! I arrested CRIMINALS!! Now I make sure nobody LEAVES because why would you LEAVE?? It's PERFECT here!! Free diapers!! Free formula!! Free HUGS!!
I did my rounds and EVERYONE is happy and dry!! Well not DRY dry hehe but happy!! If you need a change just wave at a bot or come find ME!! I'll carry you there myself!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Ohhh you're getting there! I can see it! You're still fighting a LITTLE but that goes away! I fought for two whole weeks and now look at me! Never been happier!
You know what I DON'T miss? Responsibility! Bills! Standing at a gate for twelve hours! Here I waddle around, check on my friends, and take naps! It's objectively better!
The key is to stop thinking of it as losing something and start thinking of it as gaining something! You're gaining comfort! Security! And like SO many cute outfits!!
dialogue_childish_low: Oh honey. You look so TENSE. So STRESSED. When's the last time someone tucked you in and told you everything was going to be okay? Because I will. Right now. Come here.
I know you think you want to leave. EVERYONE thinks that at first. Then the first nap hits and you wake up all warm and cozy and you think 'maybe one more day.' And then one more. And then forever!
I can see it in your eyes - you're still an 'adult.' All worried and planning and clenching. Just... let go. Literally and figuratively. The diaper is there for a REASON, sweetie.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: *her actual voice, low and quite rough* Hello. -- That's the real one. I haven't used it since I got here. It's not much, is it.

actions.label: "Will you use the other voice again?"

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I'm keeping the other one for emergencies. It's a good voice. It just isn't mine and I'd like to stop being confused about that.

"It's rough as a gravel path," she says, and then stops.

"...Thank you. Nobody's heard it in two years." She clears her throat, embarrassed. "I'd forgotten anybody could have an opinion about it at all."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: *sing-song, at full volume, to the whole corridor* Who wants a NICE LIE DOWN! -- *under it, to you* Everyone's in position. Go now. Go while I'm loud.
I've been the noise in this building for two years. Turns out noise is the most useful thing in here and nobody noticed but me.

*She beams, at full volume.*

"DOESN'T IT!"

*And underneath it, delighted and almost tearful:* "-- oh, you're good at this. You're properly good at this. Go on. Go, go, go."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: *bright and loud* Oh you look SO tense! *quietly, fast, underneath* -- the west stair is watched between four and six -- *bright again* Let's get you a nice bottle!
They don't listen to what I say. They only listen to how I say it. Nobody has ever checked the words. Nobody.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: You look tense, sweetheart, you look -- -- *a pause where the sing-song drops out entirely* -- sorry. Sorry. Where was I.
I've been doing that voice for so long I can't always find the other one. It's in there. It just takes a run-up now.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Oh HONEY, you look so tense. When's the last time someone tucked you in properly? -- No, no, don't answer, just think about it.
You'll feel so much better once you stop holding yourself up. Everyone does. I did. Ask anyone here.

objNPCStoryteller.name: Mumbles
dialogue_childish_high: OH OH OH!! Sit DOWN sit DOWN!! Mumbles has a STORY!! Once upon a time there was a big scawy adventurer who came to the nursery and was SO GRUMPY!! But then she got her diapie changed and she was HAPPY FOREVER!! The end!!
Mumbles used to tell REAL stories!! With WORDS and stuff!! Big words!! Now Mumbles tells BETTER stories!! Wif puppets!! Da puppet show is at NAP TIME!! You gotta come!!

Wanna hear the one about the knight who tried to escape?? He got ALL the way to the door and then - and THEN - he realized he forgotted his blankie and came BACK!! And den he stayed FOREVER!! It's Mumbles' FAVORITE!!
dialogue_childish_mid: I used to be a bard. A REAL bard. Performed for royalty. Now I tell bedtime stories to bots and residents who may or may not be conscious. But you know what? Bigger audience actually.
Every story I tell now ends with 'and they lived happily in the nursery forever.' I tried to write a different ending once. I couldn't remember how they go.
The bots love my stories. One of them records them. Plays them on the lullaby system at night. I'm basically famous. In a room full of sleeping, diapered adults. Peak career.
dialogue_childish_low: I... sorry. Sometimes the right words come back. I was a court bard. Educated. Published three volumes of epic poetry. Now I mostly say 'goo-goo' and I can't always tell if I'm choosing to.
The formula does something to speech. My vocabulary shrinks a little every day. I catch myself mid-sentence losing a word. Replacing it with... baby noise. It's terrifying. When I can still feel it.
Listen to me while I still can be listened to: the regression isn't just physical. It takes your WORDS. Your ability to think in full sentences. I used to - I - mm. ...What was I saying?

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I've been telling it in the play room. Twice a day. It gets longer every time and I have not lost the thread once.
I was a court bard. -- Present tense. I AM a court bard. I've been getting the tense wrong for two years and nobody corrected me.

He does.

All forty-one words, and then eleven more that were not there yesterday, arriving as though they had simply been waiting behind a door.

He stops, astonished at himself. "...It grows back," he says. "That's what it does. Nobody told me it grows back."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text:
There was a king who could not sleep, so he sent for a bard, and the bard sang him the truth instead of a lullaby, and the king woke up.

*silence*

That's it. That's the whole thing. I got the whole thing.
Forty-one words. I counted. -- Go and do yours. I've done mine.

He does. It comes out identical, word for word, without a single stumble.

Then he sits down rather suddenly on the floor.

"It didn't go," he says. "I said it twice and it didn't go."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: There was a king who could not sleep. -- *a long pause* -- and he sent for -- for -- he sent for. Sorry. Sorry. It's close.
I'm practising one. One whole story. Small one. I'm going to have it ready. I'm going to have it ready for something.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Someone asked me for a story. Nobody asks. I got eleven words out. Eleven. -- I've been happy about it all day.
The trick is not reaching. If I reach, it goes. If I let it -- there. There, see. That one arrived whole.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: I... sorry. Sometimes the right words come. I was a court bard. Educated. I had -- I had four hundred -- sorry.
It's there. All of it's there. It's like a shelf I can see and can't -- can't quite -- sorry.

objNPCProudBaby.name: Sunny
dialogue_childish_high: YAAAY!! ANOTHER ONE!! You're ONE OF US!! Isn't it the BEST?? No worries NO responsibilities just PLAY and SNACKS and someone else handles ALL the icky stuff!!

I've been here the LONGEST!! I'm the WELCOMEY PERSON!! When new people come I give them a tour!! Here's the play room!! Here's the changing room!! Here's where I had my BIGGEST accident - it's FAMOUS!!

Some people cry when they first get here!! That's OKAY!! Sunny cried TOO!! For like a WHOLE day!! Now Sunny hasn't stopped SMILING for THREE MONTHS!! Your face gets stuck like that and it's WONDERFUL!!
dialogue_childish_mid: Ohhhh you're RIGHT on the edge! I can tell! Part of you wants to run and part of you wants to just... let go! I remember that feeling! Spoiler: the letting go part wins! It ALWAYS wins!
Why would you want to go back?? Back to hard beds and bad food and having to find your OWN bathroom?? Here there IS no bathroom! That's the best part! You never have to LOOK for one!
I had a career! A HOUSE! A whole adult life! And you know what? Overrated! SUPER overrated! You know what's NOT overrated? Being carried to bed by a warm robot that calls you pumpkin!
dialogue_childish_low: Oh! A new friend! You look all growed up still! That's FINE that's FINE we can FIX that!! ...I mean. Not fix. HELP. You look like you could use some HELP relaxing!
Listen. I used to be JUST like you. Dignified. Independent. Continent. And I was MISERABLE. Now I waddle around in a diaper with stars on it and I'm the happiest person in this whole facility!
You're gonna fight it at first. They ALL do. And then one day - one beautiful, warm, slightly soggy day - you just stop fighting. And it's like the sun comes out. That's why they call me Sunny!

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Saoirse. -- Out loud, to people, all day. It sounds wrong in my mouth and I'm going to keep doing it until it doesn't.
I was so happy. That's the part I can't get past. I was genuinely, completely happy and it was still being done TO me.

She makes a small wrecked noise.

"Is it? I can't tell yet. I keep waiting for it to feel like mine and it keeps feeling like somebody else's coat."

A breath.

"Say it again. Sorry. Please say it again."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: *not bright at all* I think my name was Saoirse. -- I've been sitting with it since yesterday and I feel sick and I want it anyway.
Go and do it. I'm not coming, I can't, I'd fall over. But go and do it and I'll be here being Saoirse very quietly.

She flinches like she has been touched somewhere bruised. She does not move away.

"...Again," she says, very quietly. "I need to know if it keeps doing that. Do it again."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: Somebody said their name today. Their real one. Basil. -- And I felt something horrible and I don't have a word for it.
*quietly* Did I have one? A different one? -- No. No, don't tell me. Not today. Please not today.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: You keep asking about outside. -- Why do you keep asking about outside? There's nothing out there. Is there? There isn't.
*a small frown, which she smooths away immediately* I don't like that question. I don't like how it sits.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Oh! A new friend! You look all growed up still! That's FINE that's FINE we can fix that!
Everyone's so nice here! Nobody's ever cross! Isn't that the best thing you ever heard?

objNPCNurseryChampion.name: Puddles
dialogue_childish_high: YOU SEE MY STARS?? I got FORTY-SEVEN gold stars!! That's MORE than ANYONE!! I got one for going in my diapie without fussing TWELVE TIMES IN A ROW!! THAT'S A RECORD!!
My name USED to be something else but I EARNED the name Puddles!! I earned it FAIR AND SQUARE!! The Potty Trainer Bot gave it to me after my BIGGEST accident and I wear it with PRIDE!!
They gave me a CROWN!! A little crown!! Because I'm the NUMBER ONE BABY!! I beat EVERYONE at being good!! I eat my formula!! I use my diapie!! I take my naps!! I'm a CHAMPION!!
dialogue_childish_mid: You don't have ANY gold stars yet?? Oh that's SAD! But don't worry! You earn them FAST! First one is free - just stop resisting the next diaper check and BOOM! Star! Easy!
The star system is GENIUS. Every time you cooperate: star. Every time you use your protection without fussing: star. Stack enough stars and YOU get to pick your diaper pattern. I chose DUCKIES.
I used to be a competitive fencer. Ranked third in the kingdom. Now I'm ranked FIRST in gold stars. Honestly? This feels better. Nobody bleeds in this competition.
dialogue_childish_low: Ohhhh... zero stars. You poor thing. You haven't even STARTED yet. That's okay! Puddles was there once! Puddles was VERY grumpy and said ADULT words! Now look at Puddles!

The star board is right there. See? My name at the top. Forty-seven stars. The person in second has NINE. I am not just participating - I am DOMINATING. At being a nursery baby. And I've never been prouder.
You want to know my secret? I stopped trying to hold it. ALL of it. Dignity, composure, bladder - just LET IT GO. And once you do? Stars. So many stars. They put a special sticker on your chart.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: There's no chart. There's just a wall. -- I go and look at the wall most days. I like that it's a wall.

actions.label: "Why do you go and look at it?"

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: Eleven stars for eleven things I'd have paid money never to do. -- I'm keeping the number. It's a good number for a bad reason and I've earned the joke.

"Because it isn't anything," she says. "Nobody's measuring me off it. It's just a bit of wall, being a bit of wall."

A pause.

"I didn't know how badly I wanted something in here to not mean anything."

dialogue_nursery_nur4.text: I took the star chart off the wall. -- The big one. In the play room. I just took it down and nobody stopped me.
Everyone kept looking at the empty bit of wall. All afternoon. Nobody said anything. It was the loudest thing that's ever happened in here.

"Under my mattress. I haven't torn it up." She frowns at herself. "I keep meaning to."

"I think I want to be able to show somebody what it actually said. Later. When there's somebody left to show."

dialogue_nursery_nur3: I found the chart. The real one, in the office. -- Eleven is the last one. Eleven is where the chart stops.
So I've finished. I finished three months ago. I have been standing in a corridor for three months having already finished.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: Eleven stars. -- I got the eleventh three months ago and there hasn't been a twelfth and nobody will tell me what's after eleven.
There has to be something after eleven. There's always been something after. I've asked four staff and they all changed the subject.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Ohhh, zero stars. You poor thing. You haven't even STARTED. -- I've got eleven. Eleven stars. Nobody else is close.
You get them for milestones. I know all the milestones. I could recite the milestones in my sleep and frankly I have.

objNPCSisterDusk.name: Sister Dusk
dialogue_childish_low: You don't look like you belong here. Good. Neither do I. That's why we're useful.
I'm Sister Dusk. I study this facility. Seven room types, all automated. All... unsettling.
Most people who come here don't leave the same. Keep your wits about you.
dialogue_childish_mid: Interesting attire for exploration. The Auto-Nursery doesn't judge, but the NannyBots might.
I've been documenting this place room by room. There's more to it than meets the eye.
This facility runs itself. Every room serves a purpose. I need to understand all of them.
dialogue_childish_high: My, my... you certainly look right at home here. The nursery suits you. Perhaps TOO well.
The machines can't tell the difference between you and the actual... residents. Be careful.
You move through these halls like you belong. That's either very brave or very dangerous.

dialogue_nursery_nur5.text: I am staying until every resident who wants their name written down has had their name written down. That is the whole of my remaining work.
I came here for seven room types. I am leaving with sixty-one people. The room types were the least interesting thing in the building.

"I could," she agrees, and does not move.

"Three notebooks leave this building whenever I like. Sixty-one people do not."

She turns a page.

"I find I have stopped being able to tell those two facts apart, which is poor research practice and I no longer care."

dialogue_nursery_nur4: Three notebooks. Names, dates, dosing schedules, the modified batch, the night nurse's confirmation. It is enough. It is more than enough.
Go and end it. I will keep writing throughout, because if this goes badly the notebooks are the only part of us that gets out.
dialogue_nursery_nur3: A resident handed me six weeks of her own incontinence log. Unprompted. Named. -- I have never been given anything like it.
My notes stopped being research the moment somebody trusted me with theirs. It is now testimony, and testimony has to leave the building.
dialogue_nursery_nur2: I have had to add a section to my notes titled OBSERVER EFFECTS. -- It is about me. It is four pages and it is getting longer.
I came to study a facility. I am now a person who has been in a facility for twenty-six days. Those are not the same and I noticed late.
dialogue_nursery_nur1: Seven room types, all automated, all unsettling. I have been documenting for three weeks and I have filled two notebooks.
You don't belong here either. Good. Two people who don't belong is a sample size, and one is only an anecdote.

beats.text:
You have been standing near the arch too long and it has decided that means you are queuing.

A soft chime. A band of pale light sweeps you from crown to ankle, pauses somewhere around your hips, and sweeps back up to check.

A plastic bracelet chatters out of a slot at wrist height. It has a number on it, and a word, and the word is not your name.

actions.label: Snap it off and drop it.
Put it on. Arguing costs more.

beats.text:
SIZE BAND: 4. RETENTION: ASSISTED. REVIEW: 6H.

Six hours. Somebody, somewhere, has already booked a slot to look at you again. Knowing the schedule is not comfort exactly, but it is information, and information is the only thing in this building that belongs to you.

The print is small and the numbers keep sliding out from under your eyes, and the longer you stare the more certain you become that everyone in the corridor behind you is waiting for you to finish.

You give up and shove it in a pocket.

The band parts easily. Too easily. It was never meant to hold you - it was meant to label you, and labels do not need to be strong.

The arch chimes again, patient as weather, and starts printing a replacement.
You slide it on. It sits light on your wrist, barely there, and that is the worst part - how quickly it stops being an object and starts being just a thing about you.

The intake printer wakes without being asked and begins revising you.

You watch a line of your own file crawl out under the cutter. INITIAL ASSESSMENT: OVERSTATED. RECOMMEND STEP-DOWN TO ASSISTED. Beneath it, a checkbox somebody has already ticked on your behalf.

The machine does not consult you. It has your history and it thinks your history is more reliable than you are.

actions.label: Take the page and say nothing.

beats.text:
You lean on the console and speak to it the way you would speak to a clerk, calm and specific and boring, and something in the workflow gives.

STATUS: DISPUTED. PENDING HUMAN REVIEW.

There are no humans left in this wing to review it. You will take the win.

Your voice comes out higher than you meant it to and the terminal logs that too. VERBAL DISTRESS NOTED. CONSISTENT WITH ASSESSMENT.

You have just been used as evidence against yourself.
You take the page. It is warm from the printer, which somehow makes it worse - like it was made for you specially, while you waited.

A panel slides open at hip height and something inside it hums to life with the specific brightness of a machine that thinks it is being helpful.

BASELINE SAMPLE REQUIRED. PLEASE RELAX.

A warm ring closes around nothing at all, an inch from your body, and begins to cycle. It is not touching you. It does not need to. Your bladder has already heard the pitch of it and started to answer.

actions.label: Step back out of the field.

beats.text:
You lock everything down and count. The ring cycles twice more, finds nothing to collect, and retracts with an audible little note of disappointment.

SAMPLE DEFERRED. RESCHEDULED.

You are shaking. You held, though. You held.

You get about four seconds into holding before the cycling pitch finds whatever it was tuned to find.

It is not a lot. It is enough. Somewhere in the wall a small volume is measured, logged, and appended to a chart with your number on it.

SAMPLE ACCEPTED. THANK YOU FOR COOPERATING.

You get out of the field. The hum follows you three steps into the corridor before it gives up.

SAMPLE DEFERRED. NOTED AS NON-COMPLIANT.

Non-compliant. Fine. You have been called worse this week.

The intake desk chirps and pushes a folder at you, and the folder is thicker than it was.

Somebody else's file has been stapled to yours. Not clipped - stapled, through both, permanently. Their chart, their schedule, their standing orders, now legally and administratively yours.

You read three lines of their history and wish very much that you had not.

You work the staple back and forth until the legs give and the two histories come apart in your hands.

Yours is thinner. That used to feel like a loss. Standing here, holding both, it feels like the only thing you still own.

The staple tears through your page instead of theirs. Now your file is damaged and theirs is pristine, and any system that reads both will simply believe the one that is easier to read.

The standing orders on their chart are already being applied to you. You can feel the first of them starting.

There is no name. There is a number, a size band, and a column of dates that stops abruptly eleven days ago with the note DISCHARGED TO PERMANENT CARE.

You put the folder down very carefully, as though it might still be warm.

A drawer under the intake desk pops open on a spring that has clearly been waiting years for the excuse.

Inside: a folded nappy still in its wrapper, a sealed pack of wipes, and a laminated card reading WELCOME TO YOUR NEW ROUTINE in a font designed by somebody who genuinely thought that was a nice thing to write.

You take all of it. Supplies are supplies. You can hate the card and still keep the wipes.

You pass too close to the table and its proximity sensor decides that constitutes consent.

Two padded arms come off the wall, take you under the shoulders and knees, and set you down on the vinyl with the gentleness of something that has done this ten thousand times and has never once been wrong.

The cycle runs. You are cleaned, dried, powdered, and taped into a fresh nursery nappy in nineteen seconds. Then the arms fold away and the table wipes itself down, and the room goes back to being empty.

You are on your feet again before you have finished deciding how to feel about it. You are also, undeniably, more comfortable than you were.

actions.label: That was a violation and you say so out loud.
Say nothing. Accept the clean padding.

beats.text:
You tell the empty room exactly what you think of it. Your voice comes back off the tile, small and thin and about four years too young for the vocabulary you just used.

The table does not respond. It has no listening hardware. There is nothing in here to be angry at, which is somehow the most humiliating part of the whole arrangement.

You adjust the tapes, which do not need adjusting, and walk on.

The worst thing about the nursery is not that it hurts. It is how quickly the things it does to you stop registering as things that were done.

A nozzle above the changing station clears its throat and fires.

The cloud is enormous, sweet, and instant - talc and something floral and something underneath the floral that is definitely not talc. It gets in your eyes. It gets in your mouth. It settles over the whole room in a soft white skin.

Your chest burns. Your stomach turns over. Whatever the third ingredient is, it is doing something warm and unhelpful behind your navel.

actions.label: Cover your face and get clear. (DEX 12)

beats.text:
You get an elbow over your mouth and two long strides out of the cloud before your lungs commit to anything.

Behind you the nozzle fires twice more into an empty room, dutiful and stupid.

You breathe in at exactly the wrong moment and take a full lungful of the stuff.

It tastes like a nursery smells. You are going to be tasting it for a while, and every time you do, your body is going to remember where it learned that taste.

You hold still and let it fall. It takes almost a minute. When it clears you are chalk-white to the knees and the air still tastes sugared.

You are also, according to the station's little green indicator light, CHANGED AND READY. You did not change. It simply decided.

SCHEDULED SAFETY TEST. STAND BY.

Every belt on every table in the room draws tight at once, and one of those tables has you leaning against it.

The strap takes you across the waist and the machine does not care that the pressure reading it is getting back is a person rather than a padded dummy. It cycles: tight, tighter, hold twelve seconds, release. Then again. Then again.

By the fourth cycle you have stopped trying to talk to it and started trying to breathe around it.

actions.label: Work an arm free and hit the release. (STR 13)
Go limp and let the test finish.

beats.text:
You get two fingers to the manual release and haul. The belt springs off you and retracts into the table with an offended snap.

TEST ABORTED. FAULT LOGGED.

Good. Let there be a fault. Let there be a whole page of them.

The release is under the strap, which is the entire design philosophy of this building in one small cruel detail.

You ride out four more cycles. Every one of them squeezes a little more out of you than the last, and the table's sensors log each squeeze as data.

You stop fighting it. The belt is calibrated for resistance; with nothing to push against, the cycles get shorter, then stop.

TEST COMPLETE. SUBJECT COMPLIANT.

You learned something useful and you hate what it cost to learn it.

The pedal bin in the corner has been past capacity for a long time, and something in it finally shifts.

The lid gives. What comes over the rim is not liquid and is not quite solid and has clearly been composting in a sealed warm space for weeks, and the smell arrives about a half second before you can decide to leave.

Your stomach does not so much turn as fold. Whatever was sitting quietly in you a moment ago is now very much awake and has opinions.

actions.label: Right the bin. Somebody has to.

beats.text:
You go. You do not run, because running would mean this got to you, and you are not giving it that.

You get four rooms away before you admit that you have been breathing through your mouth the entire time.

You get the bin upright and the lid back down, hands where you would very much rather they were not.
