dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_a.desc: A pink blue latex dress #1 a.

dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_b.name: Pink Blue Latex Dress #1 B
dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_b.desc: A pink blue latex dress #1 b.

scholars_notes.name: The Scholar's Notes
scholars_notes.desc: Assembled pages from a dying scholar's research. Chrysalis is named on every page — not as a healing order, but as a kennel.

theta_scale_amulet.name: Theta's Scale
theta_scale_amulet.desc: A small iridescent scale, shed from Subject Theta just before it disappeared up the staircase. It pulses with a faint bioluminescent warmth — not the lullaby-warmth, but something gentler. +2 DEF. Passively soothes bladder pressure.

trail_rations.name: Trail Rations
trail_rations.desc: A sturdy packet of crackers, nuts, and dried fruit. Filling enough for a long dungeon walk.

dried_apple.name: Dried Apple Slices
dried_apple.desc: A paper pouch of tart apple slices. Light, portable, and easy on the tummy.

cheese_sandwich.name: Cheese Sandwich
cheese_sandwich.desc: A neatly wrapped sandwich with thick bread and melted cheese. A dependable proper meal.

berry_tart.name: Berry Tart
berry_tart.desc: A little pastry crowded with bright forest berries. Sweet, restorative, and surprisingly filling.

herbal_tea.name: Herbal Tea
herbal_tea.desc: A warm flask of mint and chamomile tea. Refreshing now, with the rest catching up a few turns later.

desert_electrolyte.name: Desert Electrolyte Flask
desert_electrolyte.desc: A chilled citrus drink mixed for Dustbreak heat. It restores a large amount of thirst and stamina.

vesper_prayer_bead.name: Vesper's Bead
vesper_prayer_bead.desc: A single wooden prayer bead, worn to a shine by thirty-one years of somebody else's hands. Warm even when nothing else is. It does not calm you down so much as it reminds you that you have already stopped needing to be calmed down. +1 DEF. Passively bleeds off shame.

cursed_crawling_anklets.name: Cursed Crawling Anklets
cursed_crawling_anklets.desc: Binding anklets force you to crawl: half movement speed and 25% less physical damage. Remove the curse-bound anklets before standing.

arrows.name: Arrows
arrows.desc: A bundle of twenty fletched arrows. Bows spend one per shot. Arrows stack up to 512 in a single bag slot and never count toward the slot cap.

short_bow.name: Short Bow
short_bow.desc: A light bow anyone can draw. Shoots from the back row for {atk} bonus damage at three quarters power, one arrow per shot. Swung as a club when the quiver is empty.

long_bow.name: Long Bow
long_bow.desc: A tall yew bow with real pull. Shoots from the back row, one arrow per shot, at three quarters power.

arcane_pistol.name: Arcane Pistol
arcane_pistol.desc: A brass pistol with a crystal chamber that channels a mage's own magic into a shot. Fires from either row at full spell-level power for 4 MP a shot. Only a mage can use it.

star_rifle.name: Star Rifle
star_rifle.desc: A long silver rifle etched with constellations. Each shot pulls 7 MP straight from the mage and lands like a heavy spell, from any row. Only a mage can use it.

emberroot.name: Emberroot
emberroot.desc: A knotted desert root that stays warm long after it is dug up. Brews red, and a little too eagerly.

blushberry.name: Blushberry
blushberry.desc: A soft berry that turns your fingertips pink. Brews a gentle red.

dragon_pepper.name: Dragon Pepper
dragon_pepper.desc: A wrinkled scarlet pepper that makes your eyes water just looking at it. Brews a fierce red that can go off all at once.

pinkcap_mushroom.name: Pinkcap Mushroom
pinkcap_mushroom.desc: A spongy pink toadstool from damp forest floors. Brews pink, but your tummy may have opinions.

bubblegum_sap.name: Bubblegum Sap
bubblegum_sap.desc: Sticky pink sap that smells exactly like a candy shop. Brews pink and a bit bubbly.

cotton_candy_moss.name: Cotton Candy Moss
cotton_candy_moss.desc: Fluffy pastel moss that melts on your tongue if you are brave enough to try. Brews a soft pink.

frostbell.name: Frostbell
frostbell.desc: A bell-shaped flower with frost on its petals even in summer. Brews a cool blue.

glacier_meltwater.name: Glacier Meltwater
glacier_meltwater.desc: Achingly cold water chipped from old ice. A clean blue base.

blue_pacifier_lily.name: Pacifier Lily
blue_pacifier_lily.desc: A pale blue lily whose bud looks exactly like a little dummy. Brews a soothing blue.

sunpeel.name: Sunpeel
sunpeel.desc: A bright rind from desert citrus, bitter and sunny. Brews orange with a restless kick.

marigold.name: Marigold
marigold.desc: A ruffled orange flower from village window boxes. Brews a warm orange.

rust_filings.name: Rust Filings
rust_filings.desc: Flaky orange rust scraped from old hinges and gears. Brews a murky orange.

springleaf.name: Springleaf
springleaf.desc: A bright young leaf that smells like fresh-cut grass. Brews a lively green.

taiga_pine_needle.name: Taiga Pine Needle
taiga_pine_needle.desc: A bundle of resinous needles from the cold forests. Brews a sharp green.

frog_slime.name: Frog Slime
frog_slime.desc: Wobbly green goo collected from a very unimpressed bog frog. Brews green and VERY fizzy.

starplum.name: Starplum
starplum.desc: A dusky plum with star-shaped freckles on its skin. Brews a deep purple.

nightshade_lavender.name: Nightshade Lavender
nightshade_lavender.desc: A lavender sprig with a darker, sleepier scent. Brews purple and makes eyelids heavy.

wizards_lint.name: Wizard's Lint
wizards_lint.desc: Glittering fluff found in the pockets of old robes. Brews a faintly sparkly purple.

moonmilk.name: Moonmilk
moonmilk.desc: A pearly cave deposit that glows a little in the dark. Brews silver and clears the head.

clockwork_oil.name: Clockwork Oil
clockwork_oil.desc: Slick grey oil drained from city machinery. Brews silver with a smell you will not forget.

quicksilver_bead.name: Quicksilver Bead
quicksilver_bead.desc: A trembling bead of liquid metal that will not sit still. Brews a strong silver that likes to jump.

honeydew_nectar.name: Honeydew Nectar
honeydew_nectar.desc: Golden nectar from the Honeydew Village hives. Brews a sweet, lively gold.

goldleaf.name: Goldleaf
goldleaf.desc: A leaf so thin and shiny it looks like a gold star sticker. Brews a rich gold.

sunflower_seed.name: Sunflower Seed
sunflower_seed.desc: A striped seed from a very tall, very cheerful flower. Brews a light gold.

inkcap.name: Inkcap
inkcap.desc: A shaggy mushroom that melts into black ink as it ages. Brews black and a bit pongy.

tar_beetle.name: Tar Beetle
tar_beetle.desc: A glossy black beetle that leaves sticky footprints. Brews black and smells truly awful.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.desc: A crumbly lump of clean charcoal. It soaks up bad smells, so it keeps a brew from going Stinky.

lullaby_poppy.name: Lullaby Poppy
lullaby_poppy.desc: A dark blue poppy that seems to hum a sleepy tune. Brews indigo, with heavy eyelids to follow.

dreamweed.name: Dreamweed
dreamweed.desc: A feathery weed that sways even when there is no wind. Brews a dreamy indigo.

night_dew.name: Night Dew
night_dew.desc: Droplets gathered before dawn, still dark with night. A calm indigo base.

sea_glass_salt.name: Sea-Glass Salt
sea_glass_salt.desc: Blue-green salt crystals from a dried oasis. Brews a steadying teal.

kelp_ribbon.name: Kelp Ribbon
kelp_ribbon.desc: A slippery ribbon of dried kelp. Brews teal with a whiff of low tide.

spring_water.name: Spring Water
spring_water.desc: Cold mineral water from a hidden spring. A clean teal base.

rainwater.name: Rainwater
rainwater.desc: Plain rainwater caught in a jar. The simplest clear base, and a very clean one.

glass_sugar.name: Glass Sugar
glass_sugar.desc: Clear sugar crystals that clink like tiny marbles. Brews a sweet clear.

bottled_tears.name: Bottled Tears
bottled_tears.desc: A little vial of real tears from a very big cry. Oddly, they make the purest clear brews.

talc_blossom.name: Talc Blossom
talc_blossom.desc: A powdery white flower that smells just like a freshly changed nursery. Keeps brews from going Stinky.

cloud_cotton.name: Cloud Cotton
cloud_cotton.desc: A puff of cotton so soft it might be a piece of cloud. Brews a gentle white.

chalk_lily.name: Chalk Lily
chalk_lily.desc: A dusty white lily that grows beside chalkboards. Brews a calm white.

rosewater.name: Rosewater
rosewater.desc: Fragrant water steeped with rose petals. A lovely, sweet-smelling rose base.

powder_puff_petal.name: Powder Puff Petal
powder_puff_petal.desc: A fluffy pink petal dusted in something like baby powder. Brews rose and keeps smells down.

dandelion.name: Dandelion
dandelion.desc: A cheerful yellow weed. Old wives call it wet-the-bed, and they are not wrong. Brews yellow and fizzy.

lemon_fizz.name: Lemon Fizz
lemon_fizz.desc: A sherbet-sour lemon that crackles when you squeeze it. Brews a very fizzy yellow.

coffee_bean.name: Coffee Bean
coffee_bean.desc: A glossy roasted bean. It keeps you awake, and it keeps you running to the potty. Brews yellow.

asparagus_tip.name: Asparagus Tip
asparagus_tip.desc: A tender green spear. Everyone knows what it does afterwards. Brews a smelly yellow.

prune.name: Prune
prune.desc: A wrinkly dried plum. Very good for keeping things moving. Brews brown with a rumble.

bran_husk.name: Bran Husk
bran_husk.desc: Scratchy husks from breakfast cereal. Brews a wholesome brown.

swamp_onion.name: Swamp Onion
swamp_onion.desc: A soggy onion pulled from the bog. The smell arrives before you do. Brews brown and REALLY stinky.

bean_pod.name: Bean Pod
bean_pod.desc: A fat pod of cafeteria beans. Brews brown, and your tummy will talk about it later.

slime_core.name: Slime Core
slime_core.desc: The wobbly heart of a defeated slime. A catalyst: it can unlock a special 'of X' potion.

ghost_lace.name: Ghost Lace
ghost_lace.desc: A scrap of lace that drifts slightly even in a closed jar. A strong catalyst for special potions.

star_shard.name: Star Shard
star_shard.desc: A splinter of a fallen star, warm to the touch. The rarest catalyst, for the grandest potions.

chamomile.name: Chamomile
chamomile.desc: Little daisy-like flowers that calm any brew. A stabilizer: makes potions gentler.

ginger_root.name: Ginger Root
ginger_root.desc: A knobbly, spicy root. A stabilizer that settles rumbly tummies.

alchemy_kit.name: Portable Alchemy Kit
alchemy_kit.desc: A folding brass stand, a tiny pot and a lot of optimism. Brew anywhere, but brews made on the road are riskier than at a real cauldron.

objNPCNiceTeacher.name: Ms. Clover
dialogue_childish_low: You're still in... regular clothes? The school handbook strongly recommends protection for all students in this wing. Just something to think about, hon.
I'm not going to FORCE you into anything, that's the nurse's department. But I AM going to leave this pamphlet about 'embracing your journey' on your desk. Just in case.
You look tense. The guidance counselor says that's usually because someone is fighting their body instead of listening to it. Her office has a changing table, if you need it.
dialogue_childish_mid: I know the uniform policy feels strict, but it's for YOUR benefit. The nurse says some students need a little extra... support. There's no shame in that. Well, maybe a little.
Between you and me? Half the class is in the same situation. The ones who aren't just haven't been CAUGHT yet. You were brave enough to accept it early!
Your grades have actually gone UP since you stopped running to the bathroom every five minutes! There's a lesson in that. About acceptance. And good absorption technology.
dialogue_childish_high: Oh sweetie, look at you! All padded up and ready for class! I'm so proud of how well you've adjusted. Gold star!
See? Doesn't it feel so much better knowing you don't have to WORRY about making it to the bathroom? That's one less thing to stress about during the test!
I told the other teachers that you've been SO well-behaved since your... wardrobe adjustment. They wanted to know if I could recommend the same program for other students!
dialogue_school_t1: There you are! I've got you down for the seat by the window. It's got the mat under it already, so you don't have to ask.
You did well today. I mean that. Most students spend the first week pretending they don't need the program at all.
If you need to step out during a lesson, just go. Don't raise your hand for it. Raising your hand takes time you might not have.
dialogue_school_t2: I moved your seat closer to the door, hon. No, don't thank me -- I should have done it the first day and I didn't.
You don't have to tell me when it happens. I can tell. I've been doing this a long time. Just come see me after and we'll sort you out.
Do you want me to check you before the bell? It's easier than finding out in the middle of a lesson. I'll be quick.
dialogue_school_t3: Somebody's due for a change. No, don't look at me like that -- I can smell it from the front of the room, sweetheart, and so can everyone else.
We're not going to argue about this today. Hand. Come on. We'll go together and we'll be back before the bell.
She does so well when she's clean and comfortable. Don't you? Yes you do. Let's keep you that way.
dialogue_school_t4: She's one of my good ones. Aren't you? Aren't you. -- See, she doesn't even argue any more. That's what six weeks of consistency does.
I don't send her to the nurse. She'd get lost. I just do it myself, at the start of every period, and then we can all get on with the lesson.
Say hello to Nurse Penny, sweetheart. -- She's shy in front of adults now. It's very sweet. She used to be so talkative.
dialogue_school_t5_low: Oh sweetheart, don't fuss with the clothes. It doesn't matter what you put on over it. Everybody here already knows.
You graduated! That means you don't have to think about any of it any more. Isn't that a relief? Say it's a relief.
Big girls dress themselves. You're not a big girl, are you? No. No, you're not. And that's fine, that's the whole point.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: There's my graduate! Come here, let me look at you. Mmhm. Still holding up. We'll get you changed before the assembly.
You know what I'm proudest of? You stopped asking. Somewhere around week five you just... stopped asking. That's when I knew.
Do you remember what you said to me on your first day? You said 'I'm only here for the term.' Oh, sweetheart.
dialogue_school_t5_high: LOOK at you! All done up and padded and perfect. Turn around. Turn around -- oh, that's a good thick one, isn't it? Gold star.
Who's the whole school's favourite baby? Who is it? It's you! It's YOU! -- see, she claps now. She didn't used to clap.
Sweetheart, big girls don't go to this school. You know that. You've always known that. You just took a little while to say it out loud.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You gave us a run, I'll give you that. Nurse Penny had to break out the strong one for you. She doesn't do that for everybody.

actions.label: "Was it always going to end like this?"

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: I'm not disappointed. I want you to hear that. You got further than any student I've had. -- And here you still are, in the same seat, in the same thing.
The ones who fight end up in thicker protection than the ones who don't. Every single time. I've stopped finding it sad. I just find it tidy.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Ms. Clover cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCFriendlyNurse.name: Nurse Penny
dialogue_childish_low: You haven't been to see me yet? The school requires a physical for ALL students in this wing. Nothing invasive! Just a few tests... and maybe a fitting.
You look pale. Are you feeling okay? Sometimes the stress of... holding it... can cause that. I have something that can help. Several somethings, actually.
I'm not the MEAN nurse. She's down the hall. I just want to make sure you're... comfortable. And dry. Mostly dry. Let me know if that changes!
dialogue_childish_mid: Let me take your vitals... blood pressure is fine, temperature is normal, and your diaper is... *peeks* ...could use a change in about an hour. I'll set a timer!
The principal asked me to track all students on the 'enhanced protection program.' You're doing great! Only three incidents this week. That's DOWN from last week!
I notice you're still trying to make it to the bathroom sometimes. That's sweet. Ultimately futile given your medication dosage, but sweet.
dialogue_childish_high: Oh, you're back! Let me check your chart... Mhm, mhm. Protection level looks VERY appropriate. You're my star patient!
I see you've fully embraced the program! Your incontinence levels are... *checks clipboard* ...exactly where we expected. The medicine is working perfectly~
You know, most students cry when they first come in. But look at you now! Padded, content, and only MILDLY embarrassed! That's real growth!
dialogue_school_t1: Come in, sit up on the table. This is just intake -- weight, absorbency rating, how many you're going through in a day. No judgement, just numbers.
You're going to hear a lot of nonsense from the other students about what the program 'does' to you. It doesn't do anything. It just stops you fighting it.
Take these. Gummy ones, so you'll actually remember. If you'd rather not know what they're for, don't ask, and I won't volunteer it.
dialogue_school_t2: Your numbers went the direction I expected. I'm not going to pretend to be surprised, and I'd rather you didn't either.
Come see me before it soaks through, not after. You're not saving anyone any embarrassment by waiting -- least of all yourself.
You can hold my wrist. Everybody holds something. There's a crack in the ceiling tile if you'd rather look at that instead.
dialogue_school_t3: Up on the table, please. -- We're past you climbing up by yourself, aren't we. Arms out. Good girl.
I'm moving you to the overnight thickness for daytime wear. It isn't a punishment. It's that you've stopped making it to lunch.
You do that thing where you go very still and very quiet while I work. Most of them do it by now. It means you've stopped negotiating.
dialogue_school_t4: Hold still. -- She holds beautifully now, that's why I keep her chart at the front. Some of them squirm for the whole first term.
No, she doesn't come down on her own. Ms. Clover walks her. It's easier for everybody and honestly it's easier for her.
Look at me, sweetheart. Good. -- She tracks faces now instead of exits. That's the change I watch for.
dialogue_school_t5_low: You can wear whatever you like over it. It doesn't change the chart, and the chart is the only part anybody actually reads.
Nine thousand nine hundred and ninety-nine turns. I wrote it down so you wouldn't have to remember it, and so you couldn't argue with it later.
I've stopped calling it a condition on your file. I call it your baseline now. That isn't cruelty. It's just the correct word.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Up you get. -- There. All clean, all comfortable, back to class. That's the whole rest of it, sweetheart. That's the shape of the days now.
I'm a Chrysalis member. LittleBigCity chapter. I told you that already, but I like telling graduates twice, because the second time you actually hear it.
You came here because something in you was already ready. I know exactly how that sounds. I also know it's true, and so do you.
dialogue_school_t5_high: Oh, look at this. Somebody dressed themselves for once -- or somebody let Ms. Clover dress them, which counts the same in my ledger.
Chin up, arms out, that's my good girl. You don't even watch the door any more. Do you know when you stopped? I do. I have the date.
Everybody at Chrysalis asks me the same thing: how do you get them to stop fighting. I don't. I wait. It has always only ever been waiting.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: There she is. My interesting one. -- I meant that, you know. Most graduates don't fight at all. You're the ones I remember.
The extra-strength was your doing, and I would do it again, and I am still a little proud of you for making me reach for it.
You'll notice I never once told you it wasn't happening. I only ever told you that it was. That is the entire difference between me and this building.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Nurse Penny cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCCoolJanitor.name: Hank
dialogue_childish_low: New student? Heh. I give it a week before the teacher has you in 'supplementary undergarments.' That's fancy talk for diapers. Trust me, I've seen the cycle.
You still in real clothes? Enjoy it while it lasts, kid. The nurse's 'assessments' have a 100% recommendation rate. And not for pants.
Hey, I don't make the rules. I just mop the floors. And between you and me... the floors in this school need a LOT of mopping. Draw your own conclusions.
dialogue_childish_mid: This school wasn't always like this, y'know. Used to be normal. Then the new principal showed up with the 'Enhanced Student Wellness Initiative.' Next thing you know, I'm ordering diapers in bulk.
My advice? Don't fight it. I've watched kids go in kicking and screaming, and six months later they're skipping to class in a onesie. The school has a way of... wearing you down.
The supply closet behind the gym has emergency diaper kits. 'Emergency.' As if ANYONE in this school has an emergency they didn't see coming from a mile away.
dialogue_childish_high: Hey kid. Nice outfit. I've seen weirder. I once mopped up after a food fight between two students in full baby gear. That was a LONG day.
Between you and me? The principal wears pull-ups under that suit. Don't ask how I know. I clean EVERY room in this building. EVERY room.
You need the bathroom? Oh right, you're on the... program. Well, the changing station in the nurse's office has fresh supplies. I restocked it this morning.
dialogue_school_t1: Hey. You're the new one. -- Word of advice, kid: the second-floor bathroom's got a working lock. Nobody uses it. Nobody checks it.
I mop this place twice a day. You learn a lot about a school from what's on the floor at four in the afternoon.
You look like you're still keeping score. Good. Keep doing that. Most of 'em stop by the third week.
dialogue_school_t2: Second floor's still open, if you want it. -- Yeah. Yeah, I figured. Nobody's used it in a while.
I'm not gonna say anything to anybody. I want you to know that. Whatever I clean up, I clean up, and that's the end of it.
You're doing that thing where you check the clock before you look at me. I've watched a lot of kids start doing that.
dialogue_school_t3: Hey. -- No, nothing. Just saying hey. You don't have to explain anything to me.
I got the hallway. Don't worry about the hallway. Honestly, kid, don't worry about the hallway.
You used to ask me how my shift was going. Just noticed you stopped, is all. It's fine. It's fine.
dialogue_school_t4: ...Hey, kid. -- Yeah. Yeah, I'll get it.
Ms. Clover says you're doing real well. -- I nodded. Didn't seem like the moment to say anything else.
I'm gonna leave this here. Wipes, second shelf of the cart, if you're ever somewhere without a grown-up. That's all. That's all I've got.
dialogue_school_t5_low: You graduated. -- Congratulations. I mean that as flat as it sounds and I'm sorry, that's the best I can do today.
Twenty-two years I've worked this building. Never once seen one of you walk back out the front the same size you walked in.
Second floor lock's broken now, by the way. They fixed it. That's the word they used for it. Fixed.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Hey. -- You want me to call somebody for you? No? Okay. Okay, kid.
I keep the cart stocked. That's my whole thing. I keep the cart stocked and I don't say anything, and some nights I think that makes me part of it.
You still in there? -- Sorry. That's a hell of a thing to ask somebody. Forget I asked.
dialogue_school_t5_high: ...Hey. -- Look at you. No. No, I'm not gonna say it. You don't need me saying it too.
Every single person in this building talks to you like that now. Every one. Figured somebody oughta just say hey.
I'm gonna keep saying hey. Every day. Even after you stop saying it back. That's the deal, kid. You don't gotta do anything.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You RAN. -- Ha! Twenty-two years, kid. Twenty-two years and you're the first one who made it past the loading dock.
She got you anyway. I know she did. But you made her work for it, and that's not nothing. Don't let anybody in here tell you that's nothing.
I'm keeping the cart stocked and I'm keeping my mouth shut and I'm remembering that you ran. Somebody in this building oughta remember it.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Hank cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCBandTeacher.name: Mr. Tempo
dialogue_childish_low: Ah, a student who hasn't joined the... ensemble yet. Don't worry, the school has a way of getting everyone to the same key. Some just take longer to tune.
You look like you could play clarinet. We need a clarinet player. The last one quit when they couldn't get the mouthpiece past the pacifier. Logistics issue.
The acoustics in this school are INCREDIBLE. Every hallway echoes with the pitter-patter of padded footsteps and the rustle of protective garments. It's like a INSTRUMENT.
dialogue_childish_mid: Music is about VULNERABILITY, my dear student! And what's more vulnerable than... *gestures vaguely at the entire school* ...ALL of this? Channel it into your reed!
I'll be honest - when they said 'the school is changing,' I didn't picture THIS. But art adapts! I wrote a sonata about acceptance. The principal loved it. The students cried.
The triangle player used to be our star percussionist. She can't hold the drumsticks anymore because of the mittens. But her TRIANGLE work? *chef's kiss* Impeccable.
dialogue_childish_high: MAGNIFICENT! Your outfit has RHYTHM! The crinkle of your padding, the jingle of your accessories - it's a SYMPHONY of childhood! Stand up straighter, let the audience HEAR you!
For tomorrow's recital, I'm composing a piece inspired by the student body. Working title: 'Rustle, Crinkle, Waddle - A Suite in Three Movements.' You're my MUSE!
The school choir used to sing about rivers and mountains. Now they sing about... well, rivers. Different kind. But the PASSION is the same!
dialogue_school_t1: New reed, second chair, and don't apologise for the squeaks. Everybody squeaks. Squeaking is just rhythm you haven't caught up to yet.
Four-four. Count it out loud if you have to -- I'd rather hear you counting than hear you guessing.
You've got a good ear. That's not flattery, that's a diagnosis. Ears like yours are why I still do this job.
dialogue_school_t2: Let's put you on the piece with the rests. Lots of rests. -- No particular reason. It's a good piece.
If you need to step out mid-bar, step out mid-bar. The band survives. I promise you the band survives.
I've set the metronome slower for you. Not because you can't keep up. Because you've been rushing, and people rush when they're worried about something else.
dialogue_school_t3: Sixty beats. That's one a second. -- I set it to that because Nurse Penny asked me to. It's how long you're meant to sit still while she checks.
Put the clarinet down, sweetheart. We're doing hand percussion today. Big shakers. Nice and easy, nothing to hold together.
Clap with me. That's it. That's all today is. You don't have to read anything, just clap along with me.
dialogue_school_t4: She keeps time better than the seniors. Doesn't she? -- She doesn't answer questions in here any more, but she keeps beautiful time.
We've got her on the drum with the strap. Can't drop it, can't lose it, and it makes a lovely noise when she's pleased with herself.
Watch my hand, sweetheart. Watch the hand. -- Good girl. She follows a conductor perfectly now. Better than she follows a sentence.
dialogue_school_t5_low: You can dress like a section leader all you want. I'm still going to hand you the shaker, because the shaker is what you can do now.
Lullabies are in six-eight. Did you know that? Almost all of them. Six-eight is the time signature of being carried.
I stopped writing you parts. I write you patterns. There's no shame in a pattern -- but I want you to notice that I stopped.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: There's my metronome girl. Sit down, hands out, we'll do the clapping one. You like the clapping one.
Sixty beats a minute is a resting heart rate. It's also a rocking chair. It's also the tempo of every song anybody's ever sung over a crib.
You used to argue with my tempo markings. Loudly. In front of the whole band. -- I'd give a lot to be argued with today.
dialogue_school_t5_high: Ohhh, look who's dressed for band! Shake it! Shake the shaker! -- there she goes. She loves the shaker.
One, two, THREE, four -- good! GOOD! Oh, she's clapping on the beat, everybody, she's clapping right on the beat!
Sing along! You know this one! Everybody knows this one, it's the one they play in the nursery wing all day long!

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You know what I heard? I heard you got out past the fence at a full sprint. -- That's a tempo, kid. That's the fastest anybody's played in this building.
They put you back in six-eight anyway. Rocking time. Carried time. I hate that I know that's what it is.
I still write your name at the top of a real part every week. I know you can't play it. I write it anyway. It's the only protest I've got.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Mr. Tempo cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCLibrarian.name: Ms. Margot
dialogue_childish_low: Hmm. Still in regular attire. Impressive. Word of advice: Don't check out any books from the 'Personal Development' shelf. Last three students who did got 'recommended' for the nurse. Coincidence? No.
You look like someone who still has agency over their wardrobe. Cherish it. In the meantime, this library is a neutral zone. What happens in the stacks, stays in the stacks.
A student without padding. How refreshing. How TEMPORARY. But while you're here in your natural state, might I suggest reading quickly? The teacher's pet does her rounds at 2pm.
dialogue_childish_mid: Library rules: No running, no shouting, and for heaven's sake, if you need a change, come to ME before you go to the nurse. I have supplies and I don't add anything to your PERMANENT RECORD.
I keep a discreet supply behind the reference desk. Don't look at me like that. Half the students in this school need them and the nurse's office has a FORTY MINUTE WAIT. I'm simply efficient.
The reading corner is the safest spot in school. No teacher's pet surveillance, no random nurse checkups, and the white noise machine covers any... incidental sounds. Stay as long as you need.
dialogue_childish_high: Shh. This is a library. ...Yes, I can hear your outfit from three aisles away. No, I won't mention it. Sit down, pick a book, and we'll both pretend that sound was a chair.
I've arranged the reading nook with extra cushions. Not for comfort. For DISCRETION. The vinyl covers muffle certain... acoustics. You're welcome. Don't make me say it out loud.
The picture books are in Section A. The young adult novels are in Section B. If anyone asks why you're in Section A, you tell them Ms. Margot assigned it for LITERARY ANALYSIS. Understood?
dialogue_school_t1: Fiction is the long wall, reference is the short one, and the third-floor stair is closed. Don't ask why. I've stopped asking why.
You may take four at a time. Most students take one and return it unopened, so four makes you interesting to me.
If you want the unabridged edition, it's behind the desk. The school prefers the abridged. I prefer that you choose.
dialogue_school_t2: I've pulled the large-print for you. -- The nurse's office recommended it. I want to be clear that the recommendation was not mine.
You've started reading the same page twice. I watch people read for a living, and I want you to know that I noticed and I said nothing to anyone.
Take the chair by the radiator. It's the one nobody can see from the corridor. That's the only reason I'm suggesting it.
dialogue_school_t3: Picture books are the low shelf, sweetheart. -- Yes. Yes, I'm afraid that is where your card says now.
Shall I read it to you? It goes faster when I read it. -- Sit down properly. On the mat, not the chair. The mat's for the little ones and today the mat is for you.
Point at the cat. -- Good. That's very good. You found the cat straight away.
dialogue_school_t4: She's on board books now. -- The corners, you see. She chews the corners. It's better for everyone that they're board.
Don't put it in your mouth, sweetheart. -- She does it when she's concentrating. It's actually rather endearing.
She still comes in every single day. Every day, right at the bell. I don't think she remembers what for, but she comes.
dialogue_school_t5_low: You may dress like a reader. You may not check out a reader's book. Those are two different things and this school only cares about one of them.
I catalogued your card change myself. Adult fiction, to large print, to picture, to board. Four lines, four dates. It took eleven weeks.
I keep your last real book behind the desk. Unshelved. Uncatalogued. It's the only crime I've committed in thirty years.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: There you are. Mat's ready, book's ready. Sit. -- Good girl. We'll do the one with the ducks, you always settle for the ducks.
You asked me for the unabridged, once. Your first week. I want you to know that I've remembered it every single day since.
The words haven't gone anywhere, sweetheart. They're all still in you. They're just under a great deal of other things now.
dialogue_school_t5_high: Oh, we're in the good dress today! Come sit on the mat, come on -- yes, hands in your lap, that's my clever girl.
Where's the DUCK? Where is he? -- THERE he is! You found him! Every time, you find him!
Chew the corner if you like. I've stopped minding. I've catalogued the tooth marks as provenance.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You went out through the periodicals window. I know because I left it unlatched. I've never told anyone that and I never will.
They took your card down to board books anyway. Same as the compliant ones. I'd hoped -- well. I'd hoped.
I keep your unabridged behind the desk still. Yours specifically. I've decided it isn't a lost item. I've decided it's on loan.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Ms. Margot cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCLunchLady.name: Big Barb
dialogue_childish_low: HOLD ON. Regular clothes?! In MY cafeteria?! ...Well I NEVER. *squints* Don't worry, Barb won't tell. But if Barb can give you advice? Enjoy that adult menu while you CAN, sugar. It won't last.
Oh aren't YOU fancy with your normal pants and your dignity! Barb respects it! Barb also gives it a WEEK! Come see Barb when you need a comfort meal after your first 'fitting.' Pudding helps!
Fresh meat! Still in big-kid clothes! You want the adult tray or— actually, sit down. Let Barb feed you something GOOD before the nurse gets her hands on you and puts you on the purée menu.
dialogue_childish_mid: Rule number one of Barb's cafeteria: EVERYONE EATS. No exceptions. Rule two: If you make a mess, Barb cleans it up. ALL messes. Yes, THOSE messes too. Barb doesn't judge. Barb has SEEN things.
The adult food is on the left. The baby food is on the right. And before you ask - no, you don't get to CHOOSE. Barb looks at your outfit, Barb decides your menu. Fair? No. Efficient? YES.
I've been running this cafeteria for fifteen years. I've seen kids come in wearing jeans and leave in diapers. I've seen tough kids cry over onesies. Through it ALL, they still eat Barb's pudding.
dialogue_childish_high: Well well well, look at YOU all puffed up and precious! Come get your tray, baby doll! Today's special is mashed peas. Don't make that face - it's going in one end or the other, trust Barb!
Oh sweetie, your little outfit is just DARLING! Look at those ruffles! Come sit in the front - I got the high chairs out for the REALLY padded kids. Extra tray support! No shame in Barb's cafeteria!
I can hear you crinkle-walking from the KITCHEN, sugar! That means you're well-protected and THAT means Barb's happy! Hydrate! Drink your juice! What goes in must come out! That's SCIENCE, honey!
dialogue_school_t1: You want the hot lunch or the sad little sandwich? -- Hot lunch. Good girl. I don't respect the sandwich and neither should you.
Extra potatoes. Don't argue with me, you're built like a coat rack and I've got potatoes coming out my ears.
You eat in here, not out in the hall. Kids who eat in the hall are hiding, and I don't like a hider.
dialogue_school_t2: I cut it up already. -- Don't give me that look. Fork's easier when it's cut and you've been shaky all week, I've got eyes.
Juice instead of the milk. Milk's been rough on a few of you lately and I'm not sending you back to class in a state.
Sit at the end table where I can see you. If something happens, you look at me and I'll drop a tray. Loud. Everybody looks at the tray, nobody looks at you.
dialogue_school_t3: Lidded cup, sweetheart. -- Because the last three went on the floor, that's why. It's not a punishment, it's just physics.
Bib. -- BIB. Arms up. There. Now you can eat like a person instead of like a crime scene.
Small bites. Small bites. I'm not going anywhere, nobody's taking it off you, you don't have to eat like the bell's about to go.
dialogue_school_t4: She takes the puree now. -- Not because she has to. Because she likes it. Don't you? -- See? Likes it.
Open. -- Open up, big spoon coming. There we go. There we GO. She's a good eater, this one, never any fuss.
Two bottles a day and a nap after. Ms. Clover set the schedule, I just hold the bottle. -- She holds my thumb while she has it. Every time.
dialogue_school_t5_low: You can come through my line in a ball gown, love. You're still getting the lidded cup, because I've mopped that floor.
I remember what you ordered your first day. Hot lunch, extra potatoes, no bib, no lid, no help. -- I remember every single one of you like that.
It's not the food that changes. It's the number of things between you and the food. That's the whole trick. Nobody ever notices the trick.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: There's my girl. Bib's on the hook with your name on it. -- Yes you've got a hook now. Everybody's got a hook eventually.
You used to fight me on the potatoes. FIGHT me. Stood right there and told me you could serve yourself. -- God, you were a piece of work. I loved it.
Sit. Eat. I'll hold it. -- I don't mind holding it, love. I've held a lot of them. You're not the first and you won't be the last.
dialogue_school_t5_high: OPEN UP! Here comes the aeroplane! -- WHOOSH! Ohhh, good girl, all gone, look at that!
Who wants their bottle? WHO WANTS IT? -- She does. Look at her go. Two hands and everything.
Messy face! Messy MESSY face! Hold still, hold -- there. All clean. Give us a smile. THERE it is.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You got into my walk-in and out the delivery door. -- Twenty years nobody's found that door. I'd have given you a head start if you'd asked.

actions.label: "They still got me in the end."

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: Bottle anyway, in the end. Same as all of 'em. I hate that. I want you to know that I hate that, out loud, in my own kitchen.
I still put extra potatoes on. Every day. She can't eat 'em and I put 'em on anyway, and if the Head Nurse doesn't like it she can come see me.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Big Barb cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCShyStudent.name: Mika
dialogue_childish_low: *stares at your normal clothes* How. How are you still in those. What's your SECRET. I lasted two DAYS before the teacher's pet reported me and the nurse 'fitted' me.
*whispers urgently* Get out while you can. The bathroom passes expired last semester and now they just... expect you to... *gestures at own padded situation* ...you know.
*fidgets* You look so... free. I remember free. It was nice. Before the 'wellness assessment.' Before the fitting. Before the assembly.
dialogue_childish_mid: *tugs at sleeve* You get used to it. Kind of. The sitting down is the worst. You can feel the... bulk... shift. And the person next to you can see your face change.
*looks around nervously* Don't go to the nurse voluntarily. Last time I went for a headache, I left with a thicker diaper and a recommendation for 'supplementary training pants.'
*barely audible* I used to run track. I was FAST. Try running in padding. Just try. The sound alone... *trails off, turns red*
dialogue_childish_high: *whispers* You too, huh? I thought I was the only one who got the... full treatment. It's nice to not be alone. Even if we both look ridiculous.
*fidgets with skirt hem nervously* The worst part isn't the diaper. It's when it... you know... and you can HEAR it. And everyone ELSE can hear it. And they all KNOW.
*blushes furiously* Ms. Clover gave me a gold star today. For... for going a whole class period without crying about my outfit. A GOLD STAR. I'm seventeen.
dialogue_school_t1: Oh -- hi. Sorry. I'm Mika. I'm not good at the talking part, I'm mostly just good at the sitting quietly near people part.
You can sit with me if you want? I don't do the questions thing. Everybody here does the questions thing and I hate it.
I've been here two terms. -- No, I'm not going to tell you what that's like. You'll find out and I'd rather you found out slow.
dialogue_school_t2: Hey. -- Yeah, I know. I'm not going to say anything about it. That's kind of my whole deal.
You want to skip assembly? We could go sit by the periodicals window. Ms. Margot pretends she doesn't see us.
Everyone else is going to start being really, really nice to you soon. I'm telling you now so it doesn't take you by surprise.
dialogue_school_t3: Hi. -- What did you do at the weekend? Not what did the school do to you. What did you do. I want the actual answer.
They're doing it, aren't they. The voice. -- Yeah. I know. Tell me something you decided today. Anything you decided.
You're still you. You know that, right? -- I'm going to keep saying it. I've decided that's my thing. That's what I'm for.
dialogue_school_t4: Hi. It's Mika. -- I know you know. I say it every time now because I want you to have my name from a person, not from a label.
Ms. Clover talked about you in front of you for eleven minutes yesterday. I counted. I count them for you, because somebody should.
Do you want to hear about my day? -- I'm not asking about yours. Everybody asks about yours and none of them want the answer. So: my day.
dialogue_school_t5_low: You graduated. -- I know what the clothes are doing. I know exactly what you're doing with the clothes. I did it too, for about a month.
I'm still here. I'm going to be right here. You don't have to say anything back, you've never had to say anything back.
Hi. It's Mika. -- ...You didn't say it back. That's the first time you didn't say it back.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Hi. It's Mika. -- Hi. It's -- yeah. Yeah, okay. Okay.
I said I'd keep saying you're still you. I'm going to keep saying it. It's just got harder to say it like I mean it, and I'm sorry about that.
Do you remember the periodicals window? -- No. No, that's okay. That's okay, I remember it enough for both of us.
dialogue_school_t5_high: Hi! -- ...Hi. You said hi first. You said hi first and it sounded like theirs.
You want to play? -- I asked if you want to PLAY. I've never asked you that. I've never once asked you that in eight months.
It's Mika. -- Say Mika. Please say Mika. -- ...okay. Okay. That's -- no, that's fine. Mika's a hard one.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You RAN. -- You ran and I heard about it in third period and I laughed so hard Ms. Clover sent me out and I did NOT care.
They got you. I know they got you. But you're the only person in eight months who made this place look like a building instead of a fact.
Hi. It's Mika. -- You said it back. You still say it back. That's -- okay. Okay, I'm okay. Give me a second.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Mika cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCClassClown.name: Decklan
dialogue_childish_low: Oh look at YOU with your NORMAL clothes! Living the dream! I'd slow clap but I'm holding my pants up because the elastic is designed for someone who's wearing something PUFFIER underneath!
Quick, act natural! If the teacher's pet sees you without padding, she'll report you faster than I can say 'involuntary wardrobe malfunction.' And I can say that PRETTY fast!
You must be new. Shiny eyes, regular underwear, sense of dignity still intact... *chef's kiss* Beautiful. Treasure this moment. I give it two class periods, TOPS.
dialogue_childish_mid: Pro tip: Sit in the BACK of class. Not because the teacher can't see you. Because when your diaper crinkles during the quiet reading period, FEWER people turn around!
I asked the nurse for aspirin and she gave me a rectal thermometer reading and a fresh nappy. I said 'But my head hurts?' She said 'Your bottom will thank me later.' Great talk.
The cafeteria menu has three options: baby food, adult food, and 'mystery.' I picked mystery once. It was baby food in an adult food container. Very mysterious.
dialogue_childish_high: Hey, diaper buddies! *air high-five* Welcome to the Padded Patrol! I'm the president AND treasurer. The treasury is just a box of baby wipes. Budget's tight.
You wanna know the REAL trick? If you waddle confidently enough, people think it's a SWAGGER. Been working on my runway walk. *demonstrates exaggerated waddle* Fashion! ✨
So the principal caught me doing stand-up in the cafeteria. My punishment? A THICKER diaper. Joke's on her - this one's way more comfy! ...wait, that IS the joke, isn't it?
dialogue_school_t1: New kid! Okay, quick orientation: the bell is a lie, the nurse is a liar, and the lunch is genuinely great. That's everything.
I do a bit where I fall out of my chair. It's not a good bit. It's a very old bit. I'm going to do it in about four minutes, act surprised.
You've got that face like you're going to be a problem for the administration. -- Good. I've been the only problem for two terms and I'm tired.
dialogue_school_t2: Okay so -- and stop me if this is a bad idea -- I've been working on a bit about the pass system and I need somebody with credibility to sell it.
You squelched. -- I'm not making fun. I'm telling you because Ms. Clover heard it too and she's doing the sympathetic head-tilt. Brace.
Everybody's being weird about you and I refuse. I'm going to keep being a nightmare at you specifically. It's the nicest thing I know how to do.
dialogue_school_t3: Knock knock. -- Come ON. You always did the who's there. You've done the who's there like forty times.
So Rowan's ahead of you now, which -- yeah. No. I had a joke there and I'm not going to do the joke.
Okay, new bit: I stand here and I don't say anything and you don't have to react. That's the whole bit. It's my best one.
dialogue_school_t4: ...Hey. -- Nope. Nothing. No bit today.
They laugh at you now instead of with you and I can't fix it and I've tried about nine different ways to fix it.
I'm going to sit here. You don't have to do anything. I'm just going to sit in the vicinity for a bit, if that's allowed.
dialogue_school_t5_low: Ohhh you're doing the clothes thing. Yeah. Yeah, I did the clothes thing. Lasted me like six days.
I had four hundred bits and now I have one and it's falling out of my chair. -- They liked that one. So they kept that one.
Congrats on graduating, by the way. That's a real thing that people say here. I've stopped being able to tell which things are jokes.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Knock knock. -- ...Doesn't matter. I forget the rest anyway. I forget the rest of all of 'em now.
Watch this, watch -- WHOOP! -- ha! Ha! Off the chair! Off the CHAIR! -- ...they laughed. They still laugh at that one.
You're my best friend in this building and I genuinely cannot remember your name today. That's not a bit. I wish it was a bit.
dialogue_school_t5_high: AGAIN! Do it AGAIN! -- fall down! You fall down and I fall down and everybody LAUGHS!
WHOOP! -- HA! -- WHOOP! -- I could do this all day! I DO do this all day!
You're funny! You're so funny! I don't know why! I don't know why anything's funny any more but you're SO FUNNY!

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You went out the WINDOW. -- That's not a bit. That's not even a bit, that's just the best thing that's ever happened in this school.
I told everyone. I told EVERYONE. I did a whole ten minutes on it in the cafeteria and Ms. Clover couldn't even be angry.
Knock knock. -- ...you said who's there. You said who's there. Oh, thank god. Okay. Okay, I've got about four hundred of these.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Decklan cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCStudyBuddy.name: Iris
dialogue_childish_low: Fascinating. You've managed to avoid the school's 'wellness program' entirely. I'm going to take notes. What's your compliance avoidance strategy? Mine failed spectacularly in week two.
You still have regular underwear? I need to document this. *pulls out notebook* Subject presents without visible padding. Estimated time to mandatory fitting: 48 hours. Maximum.
Enjoy your autonomy. I've calculated the average time a new student maintains normal attire here. It's 3.2 days. You're already an outlier. Statistically admirable.
dialogue_childish_mid: Statistically, you have an 84% chance of being 'randomly selected' for a nurse checkup today. The other 16% already went this morning. I recommend pre-hydrating for the inevitable.
Fun fact: The classroom desks have vinyl seat covers. Not for spills. For CONTAINMENT. I measured the absorbency. It's industrial grade. They PLANNED for this.
I've mapped every changing station in the school. Library: private. Cafeteria: semi-private. Gym: absolutely NOT private. Avoid the gym at all costs. I have data to support this.
dialogue_childish_high: I've been keeping a journal. Day 47: Subject - me - has fully acclimated to padded seating. Comfort threshold exceeded. Beginning to PREFER it. This is either adaptation or Stockholm Syndrome.
According to my research, the average student here goes through four diaper changes per school day. I'm at six. I blame the cafeteria's fiber content. I've graphed it. Want to see?
I got a perfect score on my shame resilience assessment. The reward was a thicker diaper with STARS on it. They called it a 'big girl achievement diaper.' I hate that I felt proud.
dialogue_school_t1: Right. I've made you a revision schedule. Yes, already. Yes, for someone I met eleven minutes ago. This is who I am, adapt.
Quiz me back. Go on. -- No, properly. If you're going to sit next to me you're going to be USEFUL to me.
You're behind on the reading and I don't care and I like you. Those three facts are all true at once.
dialogue_school_t2: I've annotated yours as well as mine. -- Don't make it a thing. I annotate. It's compulsive. You're just downstream of a compulsion.
If Ms. Clover asks, you were with me at the library from two. -- She won't ask. But if she asks, you were with me from two.
You got distracted in the middle of a sentence again. That's four times today. I'm not scoring you, I'm just -- I notice things. I notice all the things.
dialogue_school_t3: I did yours. -- I know. I KNOW. Look, you were going to lose the marks and I couldn't sit there and watch you lose the marks.
Just copy it out in your handwriting. It doesn't have to be good handwriting. It just has to be yours on the page.
Hey -- hey, look at me. You knew this stuff. Two months ago you knew this stuff cold. I was THERE. I'm the witness.
dialogue_school_t4: She's with me. -- She doesn't answer teachers directly any more. It's easier if I do it. Isn't it easier, sweetheart? -- See.
I write both. Both sets, every night. Mine in blue, hers in pencil so it looks like hers. Nobody's ever checked.
Don't ask her, ask me. -- I'm not being rude, I'm being FAST. She takes about a minute and a half and the bell's in four.
dialogue_school_t5_low: The clothes don't change the transcript. I've seen the transcript. I'm the only student who's seen the transcript.
I still do both sets. Every night. Blue and pencil. -- No, I don't know why. Yes, I know she can't read them.
You were smarter than me. That's the part nobody believes when I say it. You were smarter than me and you were only here eight months.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Sit with me. -- Good. Okay. I'll read, you listen, and if you want to say something you just say it and I'll wait as long as it takes.
I asked you a question and you looked at me and waited for me to answer it for you. -- I did answer it. Of course I answered it. That's what I'm afraid of.
I'm going to stop doing your work. -- I'm not going to stop. I've said it eleven days running now and I'm never going to stop.
dialogue_school_t5_high: There she is! Sit sit sit -- good girl. Book's open, I'll do the words, you do the pointing. You LOVE the pointing.
Point at the cow. -- THE COW! Yes! Oh, she's clever, everyone always says she's not and she IS.
She's mine. -- I mean I look after her. I've said 'mine' about four times today and I've decided not to examine that.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You didn't tell me you were going. -- Good. GOOD. I'd have talked you out of it and I'd have been wrong, and I'd have known I was wrong.
I forged your attendance for six hours. Six hours. I have never broken a rule in my LIFE and I'd do it again tomorrow.
Quiz me. -- Go on. Quiz me back, like the first day. -- ...you did it. You still do it. Okay. I need a minute, that's all, I just need a minute.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Iris cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCNewKid.name: Rowan
dialogue_childish_low: Oh THANK GOD you look normal! I've been here three hours and I was starting to think I was the last person on earth wearing regular clothes! We need to stick together!
Okay so here's what I've figured out: Don't make eye contact with the teacher's pet. Don't go to the nurse for ANY reason. And whatever you do, don't let the principal 'assess' you.
My parents said this school would 'build character.' There's a diaper vending machine in the hallway. WHAT CHARACTER IS THIS BUILDING.
dialogue_childish_mid: So apparently 'bathroom break' here doesn't mean what I thought it meant. I raised my hand and the teacher just smiled and said 'That's what your protection is for, sweetie.' MY PROTECTION???
I tried to call my parents to pick me up. The phone in the office only dials the nurse. I know because I tried every number. They ALL dial the nurse. The nurse waved at me through the window.
The class clown told me this gets easier. The shy girl told me it doesn't. The smart one is keeping STATISTICS. I don't know who to believe but the smart one has GRAPHS.
dialogue_childish_high: You... you're wearing a... is that... *gestures at your outfit* Okay. Okay. I'm not panicking YOU'RE panicking. My mom said this was a GOOD school. A PRESTIGIOUS school. WHAT IS THIS PLACE.
They gave me a 'welcome packet' during orientation. It had a DIAPER in it. And a PACIFIER. And a form that says I CONSENT to—I didn't sign it! I DIDN'T SIGN IT! ...Did you sign yours?
The hallway smells like baby powder. The ENTIRE hallway. I asked why and the cool janitor just laughed and said 'You'll understand soon, kid.' WHAT DOES THAT MEAN.
dialogue_school_t1: Hi -- sorry -- is this the right hall? I got here Tuesday and I've been going the wrong way since Tuesday.
You're ahead of me, right? Like, you started before me? -- Okay. Okay, good. I'm going to just do whatever you do.
Everyone keeps saying it's not as bad as it looks. -- Is it as bad as it looks? You can tell me. I'd rather know.
dialogue_school_t2: Hey! I'm on class three now. -- Sorry, that's a weird thing to be pleased about. I'm pleased about it anyway.
You look tired. Are they -- is it always like this? Or is it just a bad week? Tell me it's a bad week.
I've stopped fighting the morning check. It's faster if you don't fight it. -- That's a horrible sentence. I heard it as I said it.
dialogue_school_t3: I passed you. -- I'm on six. You're on five. -- I don't know why I'm telling you. I'm sorry. That was a horrible thing to say out loud.
It goes so fast at the end. Nobody tells you that. The first three take weeks and then the rest just -- go.
You were the person I copied. That's all I did here, was watch you and copy you. And now I'm past you and I don't know what to do with that.
dialogue_school_t4: I graduate Thursday. -- Thursday. I got here in autumn. -- Sorry. Sorry, I keep saying it to people because saying it doesn't make it feel real.
They've started doing the voice at me. The one they do at you. It happened in like four days, I think it happens to everyone in four days.
Will you still be here? After? -- I don't know why I asked that. Of course you'll be here. Everyone's always still here.
dialogue_school_t5_low: We match now. -- I got here months after you and we match. I keep doing that maths and it keeps coming out the same.
The clothes over the top thing -- yeah. I do that too. Nobody's fooled but I do it too, so, y'know. Solidarity.
I was going to be here for a term. Everybody was going to be here for a term. I've never met anybody who wasn't going to be here for a term.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Hi. -- It's Rowan. From the hall. From the first week. -- Yeah, that's okay. That's okay, it was ages ago.
I found my own handwriting in an old book yesterday. It was so neat. I sat in the stacks and looked at it for like twenty minutes.
You were the person I copied. I still copy you. I copied you all the way down here and I'd do it again because you were the only one being honest.
dialogue_school_t5_high: HI! -- We match! We MATCH! Look, look, we're the same! Everybody's the same!
Thursday! I graduated Thursday! -- I don't remember which Thursday. Was it this Thursday? There's a lot of Thursdays.
Do you want to be buddies? We hold the rope together! I like the rope! You go in front and I go behind and nobody gets lost!

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: You went. -- You actually went. I thought about it every single day and you actually went and I'm -- I'm so glad. I'm so glad somebody did.
I graduated Thursday and you graduated running and those are not the same thing, no matter what the certificate says.
Tell me what outside looked like. -- Please. Just the sky bit. Just tell me about the sky bit and then I'll leave you alone.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Rowan cannot help with a change this time.

objNPCArtStudent.name: Soleil
dialogue_childish_low: Oh! A subject in their NATURAL state! Before the institution leaves its mark! Quick, hold still - I need to sketch this! The 'before' is always harder to capture than the 'after.'
Your outfit has such... restraint. Such minimalism. No ruffles, no bonnet, no visible bulk. It's like looking at a canvas before the first brushstroke. Beautiful. And so, SO temporary.
You have the posture of someone who hasn't had to adjust their gait yet. Straight back, even stride, no waddle. I'm going to watercolor this moment because it WILL NOT last.
dialogue_childish_mid: There's a raw emotional honesty to this place, you know? Everyone's vulnerability is just... out there. Literally. You can't pretend to be cool when your butt crinkles with every step. It's freeing!
I'm sculpting a piece for the school courtyard. It's an abstract representation of dignity. It's very small. Getting smaller every day, actually. Might just be a pebble by graduation.
The lighting in the nurse's office is TERRIBLE for portraits but PERFECT for capturing the exact shade of embarrassment on someone's face during a 'routine check.' Burnt sienna meets rose pink.
dialogue_childish_high: I'm working on a series called 'Padded Portraits.' It explores the intersection of vulnerability, identity, and bulk. You'd make a BEAUTIFUL subject. The ruffles really frame your silhouette!
Do you ever just... FEEL the crinkle? Like, really listen to it? It's percussive. It's rhythmic. I wrote a whole sound art piece around it. The teacher gave me an A. Then changed my diaper.
I painted my diaper today. Little flowers. The nurse said it was 'not hygienic.' The band teacher said it was 'inspired.' I choose to believe Mr. Tempo. Art demands sacrifice!
dialogue_school_t1: Hold still -- no, don't POSE, posing ruins it. Just sit like a person who doesn't know they're being drawn.
I do everybody in this school eventually. It's not flattering and it's not cruel, it's just what's actually there.
There. -- That's you. Full page, edge to edge. You take up a lot of room. That's a compliment, that's not always true of people.
dialogue_school_t2: New one. -- You're smaller in this one. I didn't do that on purpose, that's how you came out of the pencil.
You've started sitting differently. Knees in. Arms across. Everybody does it around week five and I've got forty drawings that prove it.
Don't look at the old one. -- I said don't. Look, I'm not hiding it, I just don't think today's the day.
dialogue_school_t3: Half a page now. -- I've put a lot of white space around you. I don't know what the white space is. It just kept wanting to be there.
Can you hold the crayon for me? Not draw, just hold it. -- Sorry. That was a test and it was a mean one and you passed it wrong.
You used to correct me. You'd lean over and go 'my nose isn't like that.' -- I put your nose wrong today on purpose. You didn't say anything.
dialogue_school_t4: She's a lovely sitter. -- Doesn't fidget, doesn't ask to see it. The good ones never ask to see it.
Corner of the page now. -- No, I'm not going to make her bigger. I draw what's there. That's the whole entire deal I have with myself.
Look at the birdie, sweetheart. -- The BIRDIE. -- ...There. Got the eyes. The eyes are the last bit that still moves.
dialogue_school_t5_low: Dress however you like, I draw the shape underneath. Everybody's always so surprised that the clothes don't help.
I've got nine of you now. Full page, half page, quarter, corner, corner, corner. They're in order in my folder and I can't stop looking at them.
The first one's still the best. Not because you were prettier. Because you were LOOKING at me. In the first one, you're looking right at me.
dialogue_school_t5_mid: Sit down, sweetie, we'll do a nice one. -- Ugh. Sorry. Sorry, I heard it. It's contagious, it's actually contagious, I've caught it off Ms. Clover.
Do you want to see? -- You always say no. I ask every time and you always say no and I've never once made you look.
I'm going to draw you full size one day. Not what's there. What I remember. And I'm going to put it up in the hall and let them all be furious.
dialogue_school_t5_high: SCRIBBLE! -- yes! Big fat crayon, GO! -- oh, that's brilliant, that's genuinely brilliant, look at the COLOUR on that.
Look at the birdie! Look at the -- oh, she's got the crayon in her mouth again. That's fine. That's a medium.
Hers is going on the wall. Right in the middle. Higher than mine. I'm not joking, I've asked Ms. Clover and it's going in the middle.

dialogue_school_t5_rebel.text: I heard the fence. -- I started a new one that night. Full page. Edge to edge. Biggest one I've ever done of anybody.
You're standing up in it. Nobody stands up in my drawings, everybody's always sitting for me, and you are standing UP in it.
It's going in the hall. -- Let them take it down. I'll do another one. I've got a lot of paper and an extremely long memory.

diaper_change.refusal_text: Soleil cannot help with a change this time.

school_entrance_tardy_bell.name: Tardy Bell
school_entrance_tardy_bell.message: The tardy bell rings the second you stop moving.
school_entrance_tardy_bell._blocked_note: Ms. Clover walks you in by the hand now. A ward cannot be tardy.

school_entrance_sign_in_sheet.name: Sign-In Sheet
school_entrance_sign_in_sheet.message: The register has already decided which column you belong in.

school_entrance_lost_and_found.name: Lost And Found
school_entrance_lost_and_found.message: The lost-and-found bin has something in it that is actually useful.

school_classroom_raised_hand.name: Raised Hand
school_classroom_raised_hand.message: You raise your hand. The lesson continues.
school_classroom_raised_hand._blocked_note: She told you to stop raising your hand for it weeks ago.

school_classroom_desk_too_small.name: Desk Fit
school_classroom_desk_too_small.message: The desk is sized for someone a third of you.

school_classroom_gold_star.name: Gold Star
school_classroom_gold_star.message: You know the answer, and knowing it costs you nothing.

school_hallway_pass_check.name: Pass Check
school_hallway_pass_check.message: A hall monitor wants to see your pass.
school_hallway_pass_check._blocked_note: Nobody asks a ward for a hall pass.

school_hallway_wet_floor_sign.name: Wet Floor
school_hallway_wet_floor_sign.message: The janitor sets the sign down before there is anything to sign for.

school_hallway_empty_corridor.name: Empty Corridor
school_hallway_empty_corridor.message: For a few seconds the corridor belongs to nobody.

school_nurse_spot_check.name: Spot Check
school_nurse_spot_check.message: The office does its own checking when the Nurse is out on patrol.
school_nurse_spot_check._blocked_note: It stopped being a spot check when it became a schedule.

school_nurse_thermometer.name: Temperature Check
school_nurse_thermometer.message: The nurse station insists on a reading.

school_nurse_clean_supply_run.name: Unattended Cabinet
school_nurse_clean_supply_run.message: The supply cabinet is open and the Nurse is three corridors away.

school_cafeteria_juice_duty.name: Juice Duty
school_cafeteria_juice_duty.message: Lunch comes with a drink you are required to finish.
school_cafeteria_juice_duty._blocked_note: You are not required to finish it. Barb holds it.

school_cafeteria_spill_table.name: Spilled Tray
school_cafeteria_spill_table.message: The tray goes over and the whole room turns around.

school_cafeteria_kind_lunch_lady.name: Off The Menu
school_cafeteria_kind_lunch_lady.message: Somebody behind the servery slides you real food.

school_gym_relay_drill.name: Relay Drill
school_gym_relay_drill.message: The whistle goes and you are already running.

school_gym_locker_inspection.name: Kit Inspection
school_gym_locker_inspection.message: Changing happens on the bench, in the open, on a count.

school_gym_personal_best.name: Personal Best
school_gym_personal_best.message: Your body does something well, and for once that is all it does.
school_gym_personal_best._blocked_note: Your body does not do things well any more. It gets carried.

school_library_silence_rule.name: Silence Rule
school_library_silence_rule.message: Leaving would make a sound. So you do not leave.
school_library_silence_rule._blocked_note: Leaving quietly stopped being something you decide.

school_library_incident_ledger.name: The Ledger
school_library_incident_ledger.message: There is a book here that is only about you.

school_library_marginalia.name: Marginalia
school_library_marginalia.message: Someone before you left a note in the margin.

school_band_metronome.name: Metronome
school_band_metronome.message: The metronome finds a rhythm you were already keeping.

school_band_wind_section.name: Breath Support
school_band_wind_section.message: Breath exercises squeeze exactly where you did not want squeezed.
school_band_wind_section._blocked_note: You are not on a wind instrument any more.

school_band_lullaby_sheet.name: Sheet Music
school_band_lullaby_sheet.message: The tune on the stand is one that calms rather than commands.

school_art_smock_swap.name: Smock
school_art_smock_swap.message: The smock on the hook is not a smock.

school_art_finger_paint.name: Finger Paint
school_art_finger_paint.message: Brushes are for the older classes.

school_art_self_portrait.name: Self Portrait
school_art_self_portrait.message: You draw yourself the way you actually are.
school_art_self_portrait._blocked_note: Drawing yourself as you actually are requires seeing yourself.

school_principal_intercom.name: Intercom
school_principal_intercom.message: Your name goes out over every speaker in the building.

school_principal_permanent_record.name: Permanent Record
school_principal_permanent_record.message: The file is thicker than it should be.

school_principal_unlocked_drawer.name: Petty Cash
school_principal_unlocked_drawer.message: The bottom drawer was not locked.
school_principal_unlocked_drawer._blocked_note: Wards do not go through drawers.

school_atrium_class_change.name: Class Change
school_atrium_class_change.message: A crowd that is not there moves through you.
school_atrium_class_change._blocked_note: You do not cross the atrium unaccompanied.

school_atrium_pa_reminder.name: Passing Period
school_atrium_pa_reminder.message: The PA reminds everyone when the restrooms are available.

school_atrium_sunlight_window.name: High Window
school_atrium_sunlight_window.message: Real sunlight, from outside, on your face.

school_art_wall_of_you.name: Nine Of You
school_art_wall_of_you.message: Someone has been keeping a record, and it is not the school's kind of record.

school_atrium_hank_says_hey.name: Hey, Kid
school_atrium_hank_says_hey.message: Somebody says hey. Just hey. Nothing else attached to it.

school_band_shaker.name: The Shaker
school_band_shaker.message: Your part on the stand has no notes in it. Just a pattern, and a hand to watch.

school_cafeteria_bottle_hour.name: Bottle Hour
school_cafeteria_bottle_hour.message: There is a hook on the wall with your name on it, and something hanging from it.

school_classroom_spoken_for.name: Spoken For
school_classroom_spoken_for.message: A question is asked about you, and answered for you, while you are standing there.

school_entrance_walked_in.name: Walked In
school_entrance_walked_in.message: Someone takes your hand at the door, the way you take a small child's hand near a road.

school_gym_nap_mat.name: Gym Period
school_gym_nap_mat.message: The gym has been laid out for a different kind of period than the one on the timetable.

school_hallway_buddy_rope.name: The Buddy Rope
school_hallway_buddy_rope.message: The rope has evenly spaced handles, and one of them is at your height.

school_hallway_mika_says_your_name.name: It's Mika
school_hallway_mika_says_your_name.message: Someone says your name. Your actual name. Out loud, on purpose.

school_library_board_book.name: Board Books
school_library_board_book.message: Your card has dropped one more shelf, and the shelf is at knee height.

school_nurse_scheduled_change.name: On The Schedule
school_nurse_scheduled_change.message: It is not a check. It is a slot, and the slot has your name in it.

school_principal_placement_board.name: Placements
school_principal_placement_board.message: Every graduate has a placement listed. You read all of them twice.

school_gym_rope_memory.name: The Rope
school_gym_rope_memory.message: Your hands remember the rope before the rest of you does.

school_principal_your_own_handwriting.name: Your Own Handwriting
school_principal_your_own_handwriting.message: Your intake form is in the file, and you signed it yourself.

spike_damage.name: Spike Trap
spike_damage.message: A trap springs! You lose {value} HP!

healing_rune.name: Healing Rune
healing_rune.message: A rune glows warmly! You recover {value} HP.

bladder_trap.name: Bladder Trap
bladder_trap.message: All of a sudden your bladder feels more full. Wet +{value}.

gas_trap.name: Gas Trap
gas_trap.message: A strange gas wafts out... your tummy gurgles. Tum +{value}.

str_drain.name: Strength Drain
str_drain.message: A feeble trap drains your strength! STR -{value}.

tickle_rune.name: Tickle Rune
tickle_rune.message: A glowing rune pulses under your feet — a warm, tingly wave rushes through your body! Excitement +{value}.

enchanted_vibration.name: Enchanted Vibration Trap
enchanted_vibration.message: The floor hums with magical energy — your whole body buzzes and your cheeks flush bright red! Excitement +{value}.

tq_tripwire_snag.name: Tripwire Snag
tq_tripwire_snag.message: A hidden wire snaps tight across your shins! Stamina -{value}.

tq_glue_burst.name: Glue Burst
