collar_cum_slut_1.desc: A collar with a name tag that reads something deeply embarrassing. You don't want anyone to see it up close.

collar_fuck_doll.name: Doll Collar
collar_fuck_doll.desc: A collar with a tag reading 'DOLL'. The objectification is the point. Shame -20.

collar_wc.name: WC Collar
collar_wc.desc: A collar whose tag reads 'WC' with a toilet symbol. A not-so-subtle reference to your bathroom reliability. Wet resist -1. Its water-drop rune gives very public warnings.

popup_lines: {item} chirps: 'Bathroom break recommended for {name}!'
A little water-drop rune blinks on {item}.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

steel_collar_1.name: Steel Collar
steel_collar_1.desc: A polished steel collar that locks with a click. Cold, heavy, and impossible to forget. DEF +2. Its steel band can lock your posture in place.

popup_lines: {item} stiffens and forces {name} to stand still for inspection.
The steel band grows heavy, pinning {name} in place for a breath.
magical_effects.log_text: {item} locks your posture. Movement locked until you break free!
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} holds {name} rigid while the enchantment judges her posture...

lipstick_collar_1.name: Lipstick Collar
lipstick_collar_1.desc: A sleek collar with a glossy lipstick-red finish. Glamorous submission.

pullstring_collar_1.name: Pull-String Collar
pullstring_collar_1.desc: A collar with a pull-string on the back. When someone tugs it, you say pre-recorded phrases. 'I need my diaper changed!'

popup_lines: Your pullstring on your collar gets caught, and you brace yourself for another embarassing line: "I wet myself!" you proclaim loudly, unable to control yourself
Your pullstring on your collar gets caught, and you brace yourself for another embarassing line: "My Panties are Messy!" you proclaim loudly, unable to control yourself
Your pullstring on your collar gets caught, and you brace yourself for another embarassing line: "My diaper sure does need a change~!" you proclaim loudly, unable to control yourself
magical_effects.lock_text: You struggle against {item}...

pink_rubber_dress_collar_1.name: Pink Rubber Collar
pink_rubber_dress_collar_1.desc: A glossy pink rubber collar with an attached dress bib. Squeaky, shiny, and deeply embarrassing. DEF +1.

cat_bell_1.name: Cat Bell
cat_bell_1.desc: A tiny golden bell on a ribbon. Jingles with every step. Now everyone knows exactly where you are. DEX -1. The bell sometimes jingles with playful magic.

popup_lines: {item} jingles with a playful little mew.
A magical jingle from {item} makes {name}'s steps feel bouncy and silly.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

cow_bell_1.name: Cow Bell
cow_bell_1.desc: A heavy brass cowbell on a leather strap. CLONK CLONK CLONK. Zero stealth. DEX -2, DEF +1. The heavy bell occasionally clonks on its own.

popup_lines: {item} clonks loudly enough to make {name} wince.
A heavy farmyard chime rolls out of {item}.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

meow_cow_bell_1.name: Meow Cow Bell
meow_cow_bell_1.desc: A bell that somehow makes a 'meow' sound instead of ringing. Adorable and baffling. Childish +7. Its confused charm meows and moos at random.

popup_lines: {item} cannot decide whether to meow or moo, so it does both.
The bell on {item} lets out a confused magical chorus.
magical_effects.log_text: {item} makes a ridiculous noise: excitement +4, wet +2.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

necklace_1.name: Silver Necklace
necklace_1.desc: A simple silver chain necklace. Elegant but unassuming. DEF +1.

necklace_2.name: Pearl Necklace
necklace_2.desc: A strand of luminous pearls. Sophisticated and dignified — a rare feeling in this world. DEF +1.

necklace_3.name: Ruby Pendant
necklace_3.desc: A necklace with a deep red gemstone. Warm to the touch. HP regen +1. The ruby can pulse with restorative warmth.

popup_lines: {item} beats once with warm red light.
A ruby pulse from {item} sends courage through {name}'s chest.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

necklace_4.name: Amber Necklace
necklace_4.desc: A necklace with a chunk of fossilized amber. Something ancient stirs inside. Wet resist +1.

necklace_5.name: Star Pendant
necklace_5.desc: A necklace with a tiny star charm. Makes you feel like a magical girl — for better or worse. The star charm may force a dramatic sparkle pose.

popup_lines: {item} flashes and nudges {name} into a dramatic magical-girl pose.
A tiny starburst from {item} makes the room feel briefly staged.
magical_effects.log_text: {item} forces a sparkle pose: excitement +5, stamina -2.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

necklace_6.name: Moon Pendant
necklace_6.desc: A crescent moon pendant that glows faintly in the dark. Tum resist +1. Moonlit magic sometimes raises a sleepy tide.

popup_lines: {item} glows with a sleepy blue tide.
Moonlit magic from {item} makes {name}'s belly flutter.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

mystical_amulet_1.name: Mystical Amulet
mystical_amulet_1.desc: An ancient amulet thrumming with unknown power. Wet resist +2, DEF +1. Its magic feels... maternal. Its maternal ward can wake at inconvenient times.

popup_lines: {item} glows with protective, embarrassingly gentle magic.
A soft ward from {item} steadies {name} like a hand at her back.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

soulstone_1.name: Soulstone Pendant
soulstone_1.desc: A necklace holding a swirling violet soulstone. Whispers forgotten lullabies. HP regen +2, Childish +4. The soulstone sometimes gives back a little strength.

popup_lines: {item} drinks in the room's pressure and gives a little warmth back.
A violet glow in {item} steadies {name}'s pulse.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

necktie_1.name: Striped Necktie
necktie_1.desc: A professional striped necktie. Makes you look serious and grown-up. Childish -2.

necktie_2.name: Polka Dot Necktie
necktie_2.desc: A colourful polka-dot necktie. Cheerful but slightly juvenile. At least you're dressed up.

scarf_1.name: Cozy Scarf
scarf_1.desc: A thick, warm scarf in autumnal colours. Comforting and practical. DEF +1. Cozy yarn magic can wrap you in warmth.

popup_lines: {item} snuggles closer, warm as a blanket.
Soft yarn magic from {item} helps {name} breathe easier.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

scarf_2.name: Silk Scarf
scarf_2.desc: A lightweight silk scarf with an elegant drape. Sophisticated camouflage for your rather less sophisticated undergarments.

vampire_cape_1.name: Vampire Cape (Red)
vampire_cape_1.desc: A dramatic red-lined vampire cape. Sweeps behind you as you walk. Conceals panties! DEF +2. Crimson stage magic sometimes billows around you.

popup_lines: {item} billows dramatically, hiding {name} for one theatrical second.
A crimson flourish from {item} turns embarrassment into stagecraft.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

vampire_cape_2.name: Vampire Cape (Purple)
vampire_cape_2.desc: A purple-lined vampire cape. Equally dramatic, slightly more regal. Conceals panties! DEF +2. Its purple glamour can briefly steady your nerves.

popup_lines: {item} casts a dusky glamour over {name}'s outline.
Purple shadow rolls from {item}, making {name} feel briefly untouchable.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

accessories_apron.name: Frilly Apron
accessories_apron.desc: A cute frilly kitchen apron. Makes you look like a very little helper. Conceals panties from the front. DEF +1.

stethoscope_1.name: Stethoscope
stethoscope_1.desc: A proper medical stethoscope. Wearing this makes you look like a doctor, not a patient. Childish -3. DEF +1.

stethoscope_2.name: Toy Stethoscope
stethoscope_2.desc: A plastic toy stethoscope in bright pink. You're playing doctor! ...or are you the patient? The toy checkup charm beeps when it feels neglected.

popup_lines: {item} squeaks and announces: 'Checkup time for {name}!'
The toy diaphragm on {item} beeps out a nursery rhythm.
magical_effects.log_text: {item} performs a toy checkup: wet +4, HP +4.
magical_effects.lock_text: {item} catches and holds {name} in place for a moment.

combat_visor_1.name: Combat-Doll Visor
combat_visor_1.desc: A high-tech combat visor with a heads-up display. ATK +2, DEX +1. Finally, something that makes you look cool.

popup_lines: You feel something in the back of your mind dimming, as your subconscious mind interprets the instructions flawlessly.
Thousands of images flash in front of your eyes, too fast for your subconscious mind to interpret.
magical_effects.lock_text: You struggle against {item}...

tartan_bra_earrings_1.name: Tartan Earrings
tartan_bra_earrings_1.desc: Dangly tartan-patterned earrings. Scottish chic meets dungeon fashion.

ball_gag_1.name: Ball Gag (Red)
ball_gag_1.desc: A classic red ball gag strapped tightly in place. Muffles speech completely. DEF +1. Shame -15.

ball_gag_2.name: Ball Gag (Pink)
ball_gag_2.desc: A pink ball gag with a heart-shaped buckle. Somehow cuter and more humiliating than the red one.

ball_gag_3.name: Ball Gag (Black)
ball_gag_3.desc: A matte black ball gag. Industrial and severe. DEF +2. Shame -12.

bit_gag_1.name: Bit Gag
bit_gag_1.desc: A metal bit gag usually reserved for ponygirls. You can still drool freely. How dignified.

bone_gag_1.name: Bone Gag
bone_gag_1.desc: A gag shaped like a dog bone. For the pet who misbehaves. Woof.

dental_gag_1.name: Dental Gag
dental_gag_1.desc: A stainless steel dental retractor that forces your mouth open. Clinical, uncomfortable, deeply unsexy. DEF +1.

duck_gag_1.name: Duck Gag
duck_gag_1.desc: A gag shaped like a rubber duck bill. Quack quack. You look ridiculous. Childish +8.

facehugger_1.name: Facehugger Gag
facehugger_1.desc: A horrifying alien-inspired gag that wraps around your entire face. Nobody wants to look at you. DEF +2.

lips_gag_1.name: Lips Gag
lips_gag_1.desc: A gag with exaggerated inflatable lips on the outside. Makes you look like a cartoon character. Childish +5.

portal_gag_1.name: Portal Gag
portal_gag_1.desc: A ring gag with a glowing portal inside it. Where does it lead? Best not to think about it. DEF +1.

ring_gag_1.name: Ring Gag
ring_gag_1.desc: A simple metal ring gag. Keeps your mouth open. The drool is inevitable.

pacifier_1.name: Pink Pacifier
pacifier_1.desc: A large adult-sized pacifier in bubblegum pink. Soothing but humiliating. HP regen +1. Childish +9.

pacifier_2.name: Blue Pacifier
pacifier_2.desc: An oversized baby-blue pacifier. The rhythmic sucking is... disturbingly calming. HP regen +1.

pacifier_3.name: Green Pacifier
pacifier_3.desc: A mint-green pacifier with a leaf motif. Forest-themed infantilization. HP regen +1.

pacifier_4.name: Purple Pacifier
pacifier_4.desc: A royal purple pacifier. Even the colour scheme can't make this dignified. HP regen +1.

pumpkin_paci_1.name: Pumpkin Pacifier
pumpkin_paci_1.desc: A pacifier shaped like a tiny pumpkin. Seasonal shame. HP regen +1. Childish +10.

spider_paci_1.name: Spider Pacifier
spider_paci_1.desc: A pacifier with a spiderweb pattern and tiny spider charm. Creepy AND infantilizing. HP regen +1.

small_paci_gag_1.name: Pacifier Gag
small_paci_gag_1.desc: A pacifier with a strap that buckles behind the head. Can't spit it out. HP regen +2 but Cursed!

cock_paci_1.name: Adult Pacifier (Variant A)
cock_paci_1.desc: An adult-shaped pacifier. The shape is... suggestive. Deeply embarrassing. HP regen +1.

cock_paci_2.name: Adult Pacifier (Variant B)
cock_paci_2.desc: Another adult-shaped pacifier, this one even more explicit. The humiliation is the point. HP regen +1.

medical_wristband_2.name: Patient Wristband (Blue)
medical_wristband_2.desc: A tighter-fitting hospital wristband in pale blue. The text reads INCONTINENCE WARD - MONITORING REQUIRED in bold capitals.

medical_wristband_3.name: Patient Wristband (Pink)
medical_wristband_3.desc: A hospital wristband in soft pink with a tiny diaper icon next to the barcode. The fine print lists your scheduled diaper checks.

dq_clothing_waddle_diaper2_large.name: Waddle Diaper2 Large
dq_clothing_waddle_diaper2_large.desc: A pair of waddle diaper2 large.

dq_clothing_waddle_diaper3_large.name: Waddle Diaper3 Large
dq_clothing_waddle_diaper3_large.desc: A pair of waddle diaper3 large.

dq_clothing_waddle_diaper_small.name: Waddle Diaper Small
dq_clothing_waddle_diaper_small.desc: A pair of waddle diaper small.

desert_condenser_coil.name: Condenser Coil
desert_condenser_coil.desc: A dust-choked water condenser coil from an old desert well rig.

dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_lar.name: Pants Blue Cameltoe Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_lar.desc: A pants blue cameltoe male large.

dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_med.name: Pants Blue Cameltoe Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_med.desc: A pants blue cameltoe male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_sma.name: Pants Blue Cameltoe Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_blue_cameltoe_male_sma.desc: A pants blue cameltoe male small.

dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_large_.name: Pants Daddy Girl Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_large_.desc: A pants daddy girl male large.

dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_medium.name: Pants Daddy Girl Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_medium.desc: A pants daddy girl male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_small_.name: Pants Daddy Girl Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_daddy_girl_male_small_.desc: A pants daddy girl male small.

dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_large.name: Pants Sheer Nylon Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_large.desc: A pants sheer nylon male large.

dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_mediu.name: Pants Sheer Nylon Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_mediu.desc: A pants sheer nylon male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_small.name: Pants Sheer Nylon Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_sheer_nylon_male_small.desc: A pants sheer nylon male small.

dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_large_1.name: Pants Trick Me Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_large_1.desc: A pants trick me male large.

dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_medium_1.name: Pants Trick Me Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_medium_1.desc: A pants trick me male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_small_1.name: Pants Trick Me Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_trick_me_male_small_1.desc: A pants trick me male small.

dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_large.name: Pants White Girly Male Large #1
dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_large.desc: A pants white girly male large.

dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_mediu.name: Pants White Girly Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_mediu.desc: A pants white girly male medium.

dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_small.name: Pants White Girly Male Small #1
dq_clothing_pants_white_girly_male_small.desc: A pants white girly male small.

dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_large.name: Red Bikini Briefs Male Large #1
dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_large.desc: A red bikini briefs male large.

dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_mediu.name: Red Bikini Briefs Male Medium #1
dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_mediu.desc: A red bikini briefs male medium.

dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_small.name: Red Bikini Briefs Male Small #1
dq_clothing_red_bikini_briefs_male_small.desc: A red bikini briefs male small.

dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_a.name: Pink Blue Latex Dress #1 A
dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_a.desc: A pink blue latex dress #1 a.

dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_b.name: Pink Blue Latex Dress #1 B
dq_clothing_pink_blue_latex_dress_1_b.desc: A pink blue latex dress #1 b.

scholars_notes.name: The Scholar's Notes
scholars_notes.desc: Assembled pages from a dying scholar's research. Chrysalis is named on every page — not as a healing order, but as a kennel.

theta_scale_amulet.name: Theta's Scale
theta_scale_amulet.desc: A small iridescent scale, shed from Subject Theta just before it disappeared up the staircase. It pulses with a faint bioluminescent warmth — not the lullaby-warmth, but something gentler. +2 DEF. Passively soothes bladder pressure.

trail_rations.name: Trail Rations
trail_rations.desc: A sturdy packet of crackers, nuts, and dried fruit. Filling enough for a long dungeon walk.

dried_apple.name: Dried Apple Slices
dried_apple.desc: A paper pouch of tart apple slices. Light, portable, and easy on the tummy.

cheese_sandwich.name: Cheese Sandwich
cheese_sandwich.desc: A neatly wrapped sandwich with thick bread and melted cheese. A dependable proper meal.

berry_tart.name: Berry Tart
berry_tart.desc: A little pastry crowded with bright forest berries. Sweet, restorative, and surprisingly filling.

herbal_tea.name: Herbal Tea
herbal_tea.desc: A warm flask of mint and chamomile tea. Refreshing now, with the rest catching up a few turns later.

desert_electrolyte.name: Desert Electrolyte Flask
desert_electrolyte.desc: A chilled citrus drink mixed for Dustbreak heat. It restores a large amount of thirst and stamina.

vesper_prayer_bead.name: Vesper's Bead
vesper_prayer_bead.desc: A single wooden prayer bead, worn to a shine by thirty-one years of somebody else's hands. Warm even when nothing else is. It does not calm you down so much as it reminds you that you have already stopped needing to be calmed down. +1 DEF. Passively bleeds off shame.

cursed_crawling_anklets.name: Cursed Crawling Anklets
cursed_crawling_anklets.desc: Binding anklets force you to crawl: half movement speed and 25% less physical damage. Remove the curse-bound anklets before standing.

arrows.name: Arrows
arrows.desc: A bundle of twenty fletched arrows. Bows spend one per shot. Arrows stack up to 512 in a single bag slot and never count toward the slot cap.

short_bow.name: Short Bow
short_bow.desc: A light bow anyone can draw. Shoots from the back row for {atk} bonus damage at three quarters power, one arrow per shot. Swung as a club when the quiver is empty.

long_bow.name: Long Bow
long_bow.desc: A tall yew bow with real pull. Shoots from the back row, one arrow per shot, at three quarters power.

arcane_pistol.name: Arcane Pistol
arcane_pistol.desc: A brass pistol with a crystal chamber that channels a mage's own magic into a shot. Fires from either row at full spell-level power for 4 MP a shot. Only a mage can use it.

star_rifle.name: Star Rifle
star_rifle.desc: A long silver rifle etched with constellations. Each shot pulls 7 MP straight from the mage and lands like a heavy spell, from any row. Only a mage can use it.

emberroot.name: Emberroot
emberroot.desc: A knotted desert root that stays warm long after it is dug up. Brews red, and a little too eagerly.

blushberry.name: Blushberry
blushberry.desc: A soft berry that turns your fingertips pink. Brews a gentle red.

dragon_pepper.name: Dragon Pepper
dragon_pepper.desc: A wrinkled scarlet pepper that makes your eyes water just looking at it. Brews a fierce red that can go off all at once.

pinkcap_mushroom.name: Pinkcap Mushroom
pinkcap_mushroom.desc: A spongy pink toadstool from damp forest floors. Brews pink, but your tummy may have opinions.

bubblegum_sap.name: Bubblegum Sap
bubblegum_sap.desc: Sticky pink sap that smells exactly like a candy shop. Brews pink and a bit bubbly.

cotton_candy_moss.name: Cotton Candy Moss
cotton_candy_moss.desc: Fluffy pastel moss that melts on your tongue if you are brave enough to try. Brews a soft pink.

frostbell.name: Frostbell
frostbell.desc: A bell-shaped flower with frost on its petals even in summer. Brews a cool blue.

glacier_meltwater.name: Glacier Meltwater
glacier_meltwater.desc: Achingly cold water chipped from old ice. A clean blue base.

blue_pacifier_lily.name: Pacifier Lily
blue_pacifier_lily.desc: A pale blue lily whose bud looks exactly like a little dummy. Brews a soothing blue.

sunpeel.name: Sunpeel
sunpeel.desc: A bright rind from desert citrus, bitter and sunny. Brews orange with a restless kick.

marigold.name: Marigold
marigold.desc: A ruffled orange flower from village window boxes. Brews a warm orange.

rust_filings.name: Rust Filings
rust_filings.desc: Flaky orange rust scraped from old hinges and gears. Brews a murky orange.

springleaf.name: Springleaf
springleaf.desc: A bright young leaf that smells like fresh-cut grass. Brews a lively green.

taiga_pine_needle.name: Taiga Pine Needle
taiga_pine_needle.desc: A bundle of resinous needles from the cold forests. Brews a sharp green.

frog_slime.name: Frog Slime
frog_slime.desc: Wobbly green goo collected from a very unimpressed bog frog. Brews green and VERY fizzy.

starplum.name: Starplum
starplum.desc: A dusky plum with star-shaped freckles on its skin. Brews a deep purple.

nightshade_lavender.name: Nightshade Lavender
nightshade_lavender.desc: A lavender sprig with a darker, sleepier scent. Brews purple and makes eyelids heavy.

wizards_lint.name: Wizard's Lint
wizards_lint.desc: Glittering fluff found in the pockets of old robes. Brews a faintly sparkly purple.

moonmilk.name: Moonmilk
moonmilk.desc: A pearly cave deposit that glows a little in the dark. Brews silver and clears the head.

clockwork_oil.name: Clockwork Oil
clockwork_oil.desc: Slick grey oil drained from city machinery. Brews silver with a smell you will not forget.

quicksilver_bead.name: Quicksilver Bead
quicksilver_bead.desc: A trembling bead of liquid metal that will not sit still. Brews a strong silver that likes to jump.

honeydew_nectar.name: Honeydew Nectar
honeydew_nectar.desc: Golden nectar from the Honeydew Village hives. Brews a sweet, lively gold.

goldleaf.name: Goldleaf
goldleaf.desc: A leaf so thin and shiny it looks like a gold star sticker. Brews a rich gold.

sunflower_seed.name: Sunflower Seed
sunflower_seed.desc: A striped seed from a very tall, very cheerful flower. Brews a light gold.

inkcap.name: Inkcap
inkcap.desc: A shaggy mushroom that melts into black ink as it ages. Brews black and a bit pongy.

tar_beetle.name: Tar Beetle
tar_beetle.desc: A glossy black beetle that leaves sticky footprints. Brews black and smells truly awful.

charcoal.name: Charcoal
charcoal.desc: A crumbly lump of clean charcoal. It soaks up bad smells, so it keeps a brew from going Stinky.

lullaby_poppy.name: Lullaby Poppy
lullaby_poppy.desc: A dark blue poppy that seems to hum a sleepy tune. Brews indigo, with heavy eyelids to follow.

dreamweed.name: Dreamweed
dreamweed.desc: A feathery weed that sways even when there is no wind. Brews a dreamy indigo.

night_dew.name: Night Dew
night_dew.desc: Droplets gathered before dawn, still dark with night. A calm indigo base.

sea_glass_salt.name: Sea-Glass Salt
sea_glass_salt.desc: Blue-green salt crystals from a dried oasis. Brews a steadying teal.

kelp_ribbon.name: Kelp Ribbon
kelp_ribbon.desc: A slippery ribbon of dried kelp. Brews teal with a whiff of low tide.

spring_water.name: Spring Water
spring_water.desc: Cold mineral water from a hidden spring. A clean teal base.

rainwater.name: Rainwater
rainwater.desc: Plain rainwater caught in a jar. The simplest clear base, and a very clean one.

glass_sugar.name: Glass Sugar
glass_sugar.desc: Clear sugar crystals that clink like tiny marbles. Brews a sweet clear.

bottled_tears.name: Bottled Tears
bottled_tears.desc: A little vial of real tears from a very big cry. Oddly, they make the purest clear brews.

talc_blossom.name: Talc Blossom
talc_blossom.desc: A powdery white flower that smells just like a freshly changed nursery. Keeps brews from going Stinky.

cloud_cotton.name: Cloud Cotton
cloud_cotton.desc: A puff of cotton so soft it might be a piece of cloud. Brews a gentle white.

chalk_lily.name: Chalk Lily
chalk_lily.desc: A dusty white lily that grows beside chalkboards. Brews a calm white.

rosewater.name: Rosewater
rosewater.desc: Fragrant water steeped with rose petals. A lovely, sweet-smelling rose base.

powder_puff_petal.name: Powder Puff Petal
powder_puff_petal.desc: A fluffy pink petal dusted in something like baby powder. Brews rose and keeps smells down.

dandelion.name: Dandelion
dandelion.desc: A cheerful yellow weed. Old wives call it wet-the-bed, and they are not wrong. Brews yellow and fizzy.

lemon_fizz.name: Lemon Fizz
lemon_fizz.desc: A sherbet-sour lemon that crackles when you squeeze it. Brews a very fizzy yellow.

coffee_bean.name: Coffee Bean
coffee_bean.desc: A glossy roasted bean. It keeps you awake, and it keeps you running to the potty. Brews yellow.

asparagus_tip.name: Asparagus Tip
asparagus_tip.desc: A tender green spear. Everyone knows what it does afterwards. Brews a smelly yellow.

prune.name: Prune
prune.desc: A wrinkly dried plum. Very good for keeping things moving. Brews brown with a rumble.

bran_husk.name: Bran Husk
bran_husk.desc: Scratchy husks from breakfast cereal. Brews a wholesome brown.

swamp_onion.name: Swamp Onion
swamp_onion.desc: A soggy onion pulled from the bog. The smell arrives before you do. Brews brown and REALLY stinky.

bean_pod.name: Bean Pod
bean_pod.desc: A fat pod of cafeteria beans. Brews brown, and your tummy will talk about it later.

slime_core.name: Slime Core
slime_core.desc: The wobbly heart of a defeated slime. A catalyst: it can unlock a special 'of X' potion.

ghost_lace.name: Ghost Lace
ghost_lace.desc: A scrap of lace that drifts slightly even in a closed jar. A strong catalyst for special potions.

star_shard.name: Star Shard
star_shard.desc: A splinter of a fallen star, warm to the touch. The rarest catalyst, for the grandest potions.

chamomile.name: Chamomile
chamomile.desc: Little daisy-like flowers that calm any brew. A stabilizer: makes potions gentler.

ginger_root.name: Ginger Root
ginger_root.desc: A knobbly, spicy root. A stabilizer that settles rumbly tummies.

alchemy_kit.name: Portable Alchemy Kit
alchemy_kit.desc: A folding brass stand, a tiny pot and a lot of optimism. Brew anywhere, but brews made on the road are riskier than at a real cauldron.

dialogue_childish_low.text: I'm what happens when you stay. *gestures at himself — the hospital gown, the thick padding visible underneath* Three years ago I was a systems engineer. Now I can't... I can't always make it to the bathroom. *his voice cracks* They call me Patient Zero. The first one they did this to. The prototype.

actions.label: They did this to you on PURPOSE?

dialogue_childish_low.text: Chrysalis Corporation doesn't heal anyone here. The 'therapy' is regression conditioning — chemical, psychological, behavioral. They strip away your continence first because it's the fastest way to destroy someone's sense of self. Then speech. Then autonomy. Then... *looks at his hands* ...then you're theirs.

*his grip tightens* Then you're already trapped. They'll start slowly — 'routine tests,' 'dietary adjustments,' 'sleep therapy.' Within a week you won't be able to hold it through the night. Within a month... *trails off* Just promise me you'll fight. Promise me you won't end up like the others.

Every single regression is documented, measured, celebrated in their files. I've seen the reports — they grade us like... like specimens. 'Subject Zero-Zero-One demonstrates complete diurnal incontinence. Recommend advancement to Phase 3.' That's me. That's what they reduced me to. A data point.

*pulls his hand back slowly* Don't be sorry for me. Be warned by me. I'm a cautionary tale in a wet diaper. *tries to laugh but it comes out as a sob* Just... if you find a way out, remember there are others here who didn't choose this. Remember us.

The Director doesn't just run this hospital — she designed the entire program. 'Project Lullaby.' Regression as control. She believes adults are... inefficient. Messy. Difficult. But babies? Babies are obedient, dependent, manageable. She wants to prove that regression is the future of institutional care. And we're her proof of concept.

*leans close, whispers* Level B3. The sub-basement. That's where they keep the original research — Voss's notes, the RG-7 formula, everything. If you can get down there and get those files out... the whole world would know what Chrysalis is doing. *grips your hand* But be careful. The nurses on night shift aren't nurses. They're guards.

actions.label: How long have you been here?

dialogue_childish_mid.text: The point where you can still fight it or... let it take you. Some patients hit this stage and rally — they claw back every inch. Others... *glances at a giggling patient down the hall* ...others find it easier to let go. The treatments accelerate from here. They'll push harder now that you're softening.

Three years, four months, eleven days. *taps his temple* The mind is the last thing to go, and mine is stubborn. I was Subject Zero-Zero-One. The very first. Everything they learned, they learned from breaking me down. *his lip quivers* Buh-breaking... breaking me.

Stay angry. Anger is adult. They target your emotions first because a calm patient is a compliant patient. And whatever you do — do NOT drink the juice at mealtime. It has Compound RG-7 in it. I learned that one the hard way. *shifts and winces* ...the very hard way.

*long pause* Then... then you'll end up like me. Or worse, like the ones who forgot they were ever anything else. *looks at his own shaking hands* I still remember my name. My real name. I hold onto it like a lifeline. Don't ever forget yours.

dialogue_childish_high.text: Before the wards, before the nursery wing, before any of it. Just me and Doctor Voss in a cold room with a needle. They said it was reversible. *laughs bitterly, then his voice slips* ...buh-but it wasn't. It never was. They knew from day one.

actions.label: What did they inject you with?

dialogue_childish_high.text: The look of someone who's realized their body isn't theirs anymore. *shifts uncomfortably* I see it because I live it every single day. Every... *pauses, face reddening* ...e-every accident reminds me. You and me, we're kin now, little one.

Compound RG-7. Regression agent. Targets the autonomic nervous system first — bladder, bowels — then works inward. Motor control, speech centers, emotional regulation... everything that makes you an adult, peeled away layer by layer. *voice drops to a whisper* The Director's real plan isn't therapy. It's manufacturing dependence. A whole generation that NEEDS them.

Head researcher. Brilliant woman, terrible conscience. She left six months in... or they made her leave. I hear her name in the walls sometimes. *taps the wall* The ventilation carries voices from the Director's office. Voss tried to shut it down. Now there's a new wing named after her. Funny, isn't it?

*smiles sadly* I said that too, once. For months I said it. Said it right up until I couldn't say the word 'incontinence' anymore and started saying 'uh-oh' instead. *his eyes water* Hold onto your words as long as you can.

*reaches out and squeezes your hand* Then let me help you. I've been here longest — I know every secret corridor, every shift change, every blind spot in the cameras. The Director thinks I'm too far gone to matter. That's my advantage. *winks* And now it's yours too.

dialogue_wet_accident.text: *sighs heavily* You don't 'deal with it.' You survive it. Every time. *shifts in his seat, and you notice the crinkling* I stopped being able to control it eighteen months in. At first I fought so hard — clenching, timing, bargaining with my own body. Now? Now I just... carry supplies and try not to cry about it.

It 'just happens' to all of us eventually. That's what they engineered. *his expression is kind, not pitying* The first time is the worst. You think 'this can't be real, this doesn't happen to adults.' But it does now. It does here. *quietly* Let me get you something to clean up with.

Yeah. *long pause* Yeah, it is. But you're not alone in it. That's the one thing they can't take from us — we can still be kind to each other even when... *his voice wavers* ...even when everything else has been taken. Go get changed. I'll be here when you need to talk.

dialogue_childish_low.text: *speaking rapid-fire, barely breathing* This hospital is a front. Chrysalis Corporation is using patients as test subjects for forced regression. Chemical agents in the food, behavioral conditioning in 'therapy,' sleep deprivation to break resistance. They make adults into... into... *chokes on the word* ...into babies. Incontinent, dependent, helpless. And they're SELLING the data.

*desperate whisper* I have notes hidden everywhere — under mattresses, behind tiles, folded into book spines. Dates, dosages, patient logs, security rotations. If someone on the outside could compile them... it would be enough to shut this place down. I just need someone who can still walk out the front door.

*tears streaming down their face* Thank you. Thank you, thank you. *presses a folded note into your hand* This is the first piece. There are eleven more hidden around the hospital. Find them all and get them to the journalist — Mara Chen — she's been investigating Chrysalis for months. Her number is on the back. Please be careful. The night nurses... they're not real nurses.

Government contracts. Military. Private care facilities. Imagine — a compound that makes any prisoner, any dissident, any 'difficult' person completely dependent and docile. *voice shaking* They can reduce a grown adult to needing diapers and bottle feeding in under six weeks. And there are BUYERS for that technology.

The research files. All of them are in the sub-basement — Level B3. The originals, the formulas, the patient records. If those got to the press, to law enforcement, to ANYONE... *clasps your hands* But the sub-basement is locked behind biometric security. You'd need a staff keycard AND a thumbprint. I've been trying to figure out how for months.

*relief floods their face* Bless you. Here — *draws a crude map on a napkin* — the notes are marked with a tiny 'L' in the corner so you know they're mine. Check under the third mattress in Ward B, behind the mirror in the common bathroom, inside the hymnal in the chapel — page 47. Be discreet. If they catch you collecting them, you'll get 'accelerated care.'

*rolls up their sleeve to show a thin medical bracelet* Proximity tracker. If I get more than fifty meters from the central hub, it triggers an alert and they deploy orderlies within ninety seconds. I tried once. *rubs a bruise on their arm* They were... not gentle about bringing me back. And I got a 'bonus session' as punishment.

dialogue_childish_low.text: There are forty-three patients on this floor. Of those, thirty-eight are in full-time diapers. Twenty-two don't remember their own names. Twelve think they're actually children. I've been keeping count because numbers don't lie and numbers don't regress. *pulls out a hand-drawn tally chart* I need people who can still count.

Sergeant First Class Dana Reeves, 3rd Infantry Division. Or WAS. *jaw tightens* Now I'm Patient 47 in a hospital gown. They got me through a corporate wellness program — said the screening was mandatory. Next thing I know I'm here with an IV and my discharge papers are 'lost.' Military training is the only reason I'm still holding on.

*leans in* I mean exactly what I said. In this hospital, staying continent is an act of war. They put RG-7 in EVERYTHING — the food, the water, the air fresheners, probably the damn soap. *holds up a water bottle* This is smuggled from outside. It's the only thing keeping my bladder under my control. And every day it gets harder.

Phase one: document. The Lucid Patient has notes hidden everywhere. Phase two: disrupt. There's a central dosing system in the basement that feeds RG-7 into the water supply. Sabotage that and we buy everyone time. Phase three: extract. Get the evidence out to Mara Chen at the Tribune. *meets your eyes* I can handle phases one and two. But phase three needs someone they haven't tagged yet. Someone new. You.

*grimaces* I'm NOT unaffected. I feel it every single day — the urgency, the reduced warning time, the... the close calls. *voice hardens* But I was trained to operate under duress. Sleep deprivation, stress positions, psychological warfare — bootcamp prepared me for a lot, just not... *pauses* ...not THIS kind of enemy. But the discipline transfers. Clench. Hold. Focus. Repeat.

Three rules. *holds up fingers* One: don't drink ANYTHING they give you. Only sealed containers. Two: skip the therapy sessions — fake a fever, hide, do whatever you have to do. Three: exercise your pelvic floor constantly. Not kidding. Kegels every waking hour. The compound weakens smooth muscle tissue — you have to fight it with strength training. *dead serious* Your continence is a fortress. Defend it.

dialogue_childish_low.text: *straightens up with practiced dignity* Professor Evelyn Hartwright. PhD in Cognitive Neuroscience from MIT. Tenured at— at— *waves hand impatiently* the IMPORTANT university. Published forty-seven peer-reviewed papers on neuroplasticity and memory formation. *bitter laugh* The irony of a memory specialist losing her memory is not lost on me. Or rather, it WON'T be, until I forget what irony means too.

actions.label: How did you end up here?

dialogue_childish_low.text: *leans forward, eyes intense* Because every morning I test MYSELF and every morning the list of words I can't retrieve gets LONGER. *pulls out a crumpled paper covered in increasingly shaky handwriting* Monday I lost 'paradigm.' Tuesday, 'juxtaposition.' Wednesday... *studies the paper* ...I couldn't read what I wrote on Wednesday. *paper trembles in their hand* I need to know OTHER people still have the words. That they still EXIST somewhere.

actions.label: They exist. I still have them.

dialogue_childish_low.text: Compound RG-7. It targets the neural pathways in reverse order of acquisition — last learned, first lost. Complex vocabulary goes before simple words. Abstract reasoning before concrete. And... *voice drops* ...voluntary sphincter control is apparently one of the FIRST complex motor skills to degrade. I know this because I STUDIED THIS EXACT MECHANISM in rats and now— *chokes on the irony* —now I'm the rat.

*grips your hand with academic intensity* Document me. Write down everything I say while I can still say it. The compound, the progression, the neurological mechanism — I can explain all of it RIGHT NOW because today is a good day. Tomorrow might not be. *starts talking rapidly* RG-7 binds to acetylcholine receptors in the hippocampus and systematically— *write this down, WRITE THIS DOWN*

I was RECRUITED. Chrysalis offered a research grant — two million dollars to study 'revolutionary neuroplasticity treatments.' I was so focused on the science I didn't read the fine print. *laughs hollowly* The fine print said 'voluntary test subject' in subsection 14, paragraph C. My own SIGNATURE put me in this chair, in this diaper, losing everything I spent forty years building.

*eyes fill with tears of relief* Thank you. *squeezes your hand* Come back tomorrow. Come back every day. Ask me a hard word and make me define it. It's the only exercise that slows the degradation. Yesterday the patient in Ward C forgot what 'blue' was. BLUE. A word toddlers know. *whispers fiercely* I will NOT forget 'blue.' I will NOT.

"When we make our move � the tunnel � you need to be dry. Sound carries down there. Wet fabric squeaks. Smell carries further."

Riley half-drags you down the hall, checking corners with practiced speed. They shove you into the laundry alcove and yank the curtain closed.
"Okay. Okay."
They're breathing fast � not from exertion, from adrenaline.
"Supply closet � bottom shelf � there's cleaning wipes and a spare gown. I'll get them."
They pause at the curtain.
"Don't move. Don't let anyone see you. If an orderly finds you like this, they flag it � and flagged patients get extra 'supervision.' That means cameras. Cameras mean no escape."

"Clean up WHERE? The bathroom is past two camera zones and Orderly Marcus is doing his rounds."
Riley's eyes are calculating trajectories, timing, risk.
"Laundry alcove. Now. I've got wipes stashed there."
They check the corridor � it's clear, but not for long.
"The SMELL, okay? That's the clock we're racing. Orderlies follow it like sharks follow blood. We have maybe two minutes before someone comes to 'help' you, and 'help' means a chart note and increased dosage."
They pull you toward the alcove.
"Move your feet. I'll handle the rest."

"HEY." Riley grabs your shoulders. Firm. Not gentle.
"I get it. I've been there. Day forty-one, right in the middle of the common room. Everyone saw. I wanted to die."
Their grip tightens.
"But I DIDN'T die. I cleaned up, I shut down the shame, and I survived. That's what we DO in here."
They pull you forward.
"You can fall apart later. Right now, we need to move before the smell brings orderlies and someone decides you need to be transferred to the 'special care' wing."
Their voice drops.
"Trust me � you do NOT want to see the special care wing."

Riley returns with wipes, a gown, and a small bottle of hand sanitizer. They stand guard outside the curtain while you clean up, narrating an imaginary argument with an orderly about pudding cups to cover any sounds.
When you emerge, Riley gives you a once-over.
"Better. Not perfect � the smell lingers. Stay near the kitchen for the next hour. The cooking smells will mask it."
They hesitate, then add � quieter, almost human:
"It gets easier. Not the... that part never gets easier. But the not-falling-apart-afterwards part. That gets easier."
They check the corridor.
"Kitchen. One hour. Then find me in the common room."

dialogue_childish_low.text:
"Thirty-four years. Started at St. Catherine's Memorial — real hospital, real doctors, real patients who went home."
He leans on his mop.
"Then Chrysalis Corporation bought the place. New name. New paint. New 'research programs.'"
His eyes are steady and heavy.
"Same building, though. Same bones. Same secrets."
He pauses.
"A building this old accumulates a lot of secrets. Especially when the new owners don't bother learning the old blueprints."

"What's happening?"
Pete glances at the security camera in the corner — a habitual check.
"They call it 'regression therapy.' Say they're helping people. New treatment for PTSD, anxiety, whatever diagnosis they can stamp on a chart."
He wrings his mop like he's wringing a neck.
"What I SEE — mopping these floors at 3 AM when nobody thinks the janitor notices — is people going into the sublevels walking and talking, and coming out in diapers."
He meets your eyes.
"That's what's happening. Has been for nine years. And I'm the only one left who remembers what this place was before."

"Stay? Where else would I go? I'm seventy-one. No family. This hospital is the only life I've got."
He dunks the mop meditatively.
"But also... I stay because someone needs to remember. Someone needs to know where the bodies are buried."
A pause.
"That's a figure of speech. Mostly."
He glances at the morgue door down the corridor.
"...mostly."

actions.label: Pete. The morgue. What's down there?
I think you're braver than you let on.

dialogue_childish_low.text:
Pete checks the corridor. Empty. He speaks low and quick.
"Alright. Listen. This building was built in 1952. There's a whole network underneath — service tunnels, coal delivery passages, old boiler access routes."
He kneels and taps a floor tile with the mop handle. Hollow.
"Watch where I mop. The tiles are different in some places. Original St. Catherine's tiles are slightly darker. Chipped edges. They mark the old passages underneath."
He stands, knees creaking.
"East corridor, by the morgue stairs. Third row from the wall. Loose tile. Lift it and there's a maintenance hatch."
He pushes his bucket away.
"I've never told anyone that directly. So either you're trustworthy or I'm getting senile."
A thin smile.
"Maybe both. Watch your step down there — and I mean that literally. It's dark."

actions.label: Thank you, Pete. I won't forget this.

dialogue_childish_low.text:
"Me?" He chuckles — warm and sad.
"I'm seventy-one with two bad knees and a heart murmur. I'd slow you down and we'd both get caught."
He pats your shoulder.
"Besides. Someone needs to stay and keep mopping. Keep watching. Keep the old paths clear for the next person who needs them."
His hand tightens briefly on your shoulder.
"Get out. Tell someone. ANYONE. What they're doing in here."
He picks up his mop.
"Now go. Before the cameras loop back."

Pete nods once. No drama. No tears. Just a working man who's done what he can.
"One more thing."
He mops a slow arc on the floor — it almost looks like an arrow, pointing east.
"The old paths go deeper than the tunnels. Sublevel 2 has rooms that aren't on any blueprint Chrysalis has. I know because I still clean them. Out of habit."
He tips an invisible hat.
"Good luck, kid. And remember: if anyone asks, I was just an old man mopping."
He shuffles away, humming something that might be a hymn, mop swishing in gentle arcs that — if you follow them — trace a perfect path to the east corridor.

dialogue_childish_low.text:
"Four years ago, Chrysalis Corporation took over hospital management. Within six months, the entire wing was converted to what they call 'regression therapy.'"
He speaks quickly, quietly.
"I've watched patients come in with depression, anxiety, insomnia — treatable conditions. Within weeks, they can't feed themselves. Within months, they don't remember their own names."
His hand clenches.
"The staff call it treatment. The paperwork calls it treatment. But I've sat with these people. I've held their hands while they forgot who they were."
He looks at you.
"That's not medicine. That's destruction."

"I've filed complaints. Seventeen formal complaints with the diocesan office. They disappear."
Father Brennan's voice is tight with controlled fury.
"I contacted the state health board — twice. Both times, the hospital passed 'surprise inspections' that were clearly announced in advance."
He pulls a small notebook from his breast pocket.
"So I started documenting everything myself. Patient names, admission dates, treatment timelines, behavioral changes. Four years of records."
He taps the notebook.
"I also slip information to patients through prayer cards. Guard schedules, security codes, camera blind spots. Anything that might help someone get to the truth."
He meets your eyes.
"The prayer cards are the one thing they can't stop. Freedom of religion. Even Chrysalis has to let a chaplain distribute scripture."

dialogue_childish_low.text:
"Dangerous? Of course it's dangerous."
Father Brennan's mouth twists.
"Sister Maria, the previous chaplain — she asked too many questions. One day she was reassigned to a parish in rural Alaska. Just like that. No discussion, no appeal."
He adjusts his collar.
"If I leave, they'll replace me with someone compliant. And the patients lose their one avenue of unmonitored contact."
He taps the prayer cards in his pocket.
"I'm more useful in here than out there. Out there, I'm a conspiracy theorist in a collar. In here, I'm infrastructure."
A grim smile.
"Besides. I took vows. To serve the suffering. I can't think of anyone suffering more than the people in this building."

"I need physical evidence. Documents, vials, internal memos — anything that proves the treatments are designed to cause regression, not cure it."
He speaks like a man who's rehearsed this pitch many times.
"I have a contact at the state attorney general's office. A former parishioner. She'll act — but only with irrefutable proof."
He hands you a prayer card. This one has a hand-drawn map on the back.
"The records office on the third floor. The pharmaceutical storage in Lab C. The research data in Dr. Keane's office."
He grips your arm — hard.
"Get me something from ANY of those locations and I can get it to the outside within 24 hours. I mail documents in the chapel's outgoing post — the hospital doesn't screen religious correspondence."

"If you're caught..."
Father Brennan pauses.
"Tell them you were confused. Disoriented. Blame the treatments — they'll believe it because they KNOW what the compound does."
He pulls another card from his pocket.
"This one has the schedule for Nurse Rachel's rounds. She's the most dangerous. Avoids her."
He lowers his voice further.
"If things go truly wrong — get to the chapel. I have a key to the sacristy. It locks from the inside. Even hospital security won't break down a church door."
A bitter laugh.
"The one advantage of working for a higher authority — they're still afraid of the optics."

Father Brennan straightens up, and the transformation is immediate — the steel leaves his eyes, replaced by warm pastoral concern. His shoulders soften. His hands fold gently.
"Well, I hope that prayer brought you some comfort, my child."
His voice is perfectly, theatrically soothing — for the benefit of the security camera fifteen feet away.
"God bless you. I'll visit again tomorrow."
He pats your shoulder and shuffles away, the picture of a kindly, harmless old priest.

He's counting on you.

"What they're doing here."
Father Brennan is very still.
"I've been a chaplain for eleven years. In the first seven, this was a normal hospital. Difficult patients, yes, but normal care."
He lowers his voice.
"Four years ago, new management took over. Chrysalis Corporation. The patient population changed. The treatments changed. The outcomes..."
He stares at his hands.
"I've watched people come in whole and leave in pieces. I've held the hands of patients who forgot their own names while nurses smiled and called it 'progress.'"
His jaw tightens.
"I've filed seventeen complaints with the diocesan office. They all disappeared."

"Then let me help you remember."
Father Brennan takes your hand — warm, calloused, steady.
"Tell me something about yourself from before. Anything. A favorite food. A song. A person you loved."
He waits patiently.
"The compound — the treatments — they target memory and executive function. But emotional memory is stored differently. Deeper."
He taps his chest.
"They can erode what you KNOW. But what you FEEL is harder to erase."
He squeezes your hand.
"Hold onto that. Whatever makes you feel like yourself — hold onto it with everything you have."

actions.label: How do you know about the compound?

dialogue_childish_mid.text:
Father Brennan hands you the prayer card. On the front: a printed prayer to St. Jude, patron saint of lost causes.
"Fitting, isn't it?"
On the back, between the lines of the printed text, tiny handwritten notes:
'Night shift skeleton crew: 2-4 AM. Camera blind spot: east stairwell B2-B3. Records clerk leaves filing room unlocked during smoke breaks — 10:15 AM, 3:30 PM.'
Father Brennan clasps his hands as if in prayer.
"St. Jude has always been generous with his guidance. Very... specific guidance."

actions.label: You're more than a chaplain, aren't you?

dialogue_childish_mid.text:
"Why do I stay? Because someone has to bear witness."
Father Brennan's eyes are hard.
"Every patient I visit. Every hand I hold. Every name I learn before they forget it themselves. I write them down. All of them."
He taps his breast pocket.
"I have a journal. Eleven years of entries. Four years of... of what this place has become."
He meets your eyes.
"When this ends — and it WILL end — someone will need to testify. Someone will need to remember what was done here."
He stands.
"I intend to be that someone."

Father Brennan stands and adjusts his collar.
"I'll be back tomorrow. Same time. I always am."
He pauses.
"If you need to reach me outside visiting hours — the chapel is open 24 hours. Hospital policy. They can't restrict access to spiritual care."
A knowing look.
"I keep extra prayer cards in the hymnal rack. Third row, left side."
He walks away, hands folded behind his back, every inch the harmless, doddering chaplain. But his steps are deliberate, and he counts the security cameras as he passes each one.

dialogue_childish_high.text:
A man in a black clerical shirt and Roman collar kneels to your eye level. His face is weathered, kind, and deeply sad.
"Hello, little one. I'm Father Brennan. The hospital chaplain."
He holds up a small laminated prayer card decorated with a dove.
"Would you like a blessing today? I've been visiting the patients in this ward."

actions.label: Find the adult meaning under the nursery talk.

dialogue_childish_high.text:
Father Brennan makes the sign of the cross in the air and places his hand gently on your head.
"The Lord bless you and keep you. The Lord make His face shine upon you and give you peace."
His voice is a warm baritone that fills the sterile corridor with something almost like home.
"There."
He presses the prayer card into your hand.
"Keep this with you. Read it when you feel afraid."
He leans closer and whispers:
"Read the BACK, too. When you're alone."

You flip the card over. On the front: Psalm 23 in elegant script. On the back, in tiny handwriting squeezed between the printed text:
'Ward B security code changes Tuesdays. Old codes work for 6 hrs after midnight. Staff break room has unlocked filing cabinet — patient transfer records inside.'
Father Brennan watches you read, his expression perfectly serene.
"Prayer brings great comfort in difficult times, wouldn't you say?"

"I distribute prayer cards to every patient in this hospital. It's my calling."
His eyes are steady, warm, and completely unreadable.
"Sometimes the Lord works in mysterious ways. Sometimes He puts the right words in front of the right eyes at the right time."
He adjusts his collar.
"I would never presume to add to the Lord's scripture, of course. That would be quite inappropriate for a chaplain."
The faintest hint of a smile.
"But I do have terrible handwriting. Things end up in odd places."

"That's perfectly all right. Not everyone wants a blessing, and that's between you and the Almighty."
He places the prayer card on the table beside you.
"I'll leave this here, just in case. Sometimes it helps to have something to hold onto."
He stands, smooths his shirt, and pauses.
"I visit this ward every day. If you ever need someone to talk to — or just to sit quietly with — I'm here."
His eyes linger on you with a sadness that seems far too heavy for a simple hospital chaplain.

Father Brennan stands and brushes off his knees.
"I have more visits to make. Mrs. Chen in Room 14 likes when I read to her. She doesn't understand the words anymore, but she likes the sound."
He pauses.
"Keep that card safe. And remember — you are loved. Not by the hospital. Not by the staff. By something much bigger and much kinder than this place."
He walks down the corridor, stopping at each room, distributing prayer cards to patients who can barely hold them.

dialogue_wet_accident.text:
Father Brennan rounds the corner and spots you. His eyes drop. He doesn't gasp, doesn't stare, doesn't hesitate.
In one smooth motion, he removes his black suit jacket and drapes it around your waist, tying the sleeves in a neat knot. The fabric covers everything.
Then he simply stands beside you. Close. Present.
He says nothing for a long moment.

skill_check.label: Father Thomas Brennan: Keep control of the moment.

partial_effects.message: Skillcheck partial: Father Thomas Brennan gave you an incomplete lead.

actions.label: Aren't you going to say something?

dialogue_wet_accident.text:
"Don't thank me. This is the bare minimum of human decency."
His voice is quiet, firm, furious — not at you.
"In a just world, nobody would need to thank a stranger for a jacket. In a just world, this wouldn't be happening to you."
He adjusts the jacket around your waist, ensuring coverage.
"I've given away four jackets this month alone. The dry cleaner at St. Catherine's must think I have a problem."
The tiniest flicker of humor in his eyes.
"I keep buying new ones. Black. Easy to replace. Hard to stain."

Father Brennan stands beside you in silence. Not uncomfortable silence — companionable silence. The silence of someone who has sat with the dying, the grieving, the broken.
After a full minute, he speaks quietly.
"You know, in seminary, they taught us about kenosis. Self-emptying. The idea that Christ emptied himself of divine power to become human — vulnerable, mortal, subject to every indignity of the flesh."
A pause.
"The body is not the enemy. The body is mortal and fragile and sometimes it fails us. That's not sin. That's not shame."
He puts his hand on your shoulder — warm, steady.
"The people who made this happen to you... THAT is sin."

actions.label: I don't feel very dignified right now.

dialogue_wet_accident.text:
"What would you like me to say?"
Father Brennan's voice is gentle.
"That it's okay? You know that. That it's not your fault? You know that too."
He folds his arms.
"I've learned, after thirty years as a priest, that sometimes words are less useful than presence. Sometimes the most dignifying thing you can do for someone is stand next to them and not make it a thing."
He glances at you.
"So I'm standing next to you. And it's not a thing."
A beat.
"Unless you want to talk. In which case, it can be a thing. I'm flexible."

actions.label: How do you stay so calm?

dialogue_wet_accident.text:
"Every day. Multiple times a day."
Father Brennan's calm fractures — just barely.
"I have a route. Start in Ward A, work through to Ward C. Every visit, at least three patients need... need a jacket. Or a blanket. Or just someone to stand between them and the corridor."
His voice tightens.
"The staff don't help. They stand there with clipboards and make NOTES. 'Patient exhibited incontinence episode at 14:32.' Like they're documenting an experiment."
He steadies himself.
"Because that's exactly what they're doing."
He pulls a fresh prayer card from his shirt pocket and tucks it into the jacket pocket.
"There's information in there. For when you're ready."

"Dignity is not something you earn. It's not something that can be taken from you. It is inherent in your existence."
Father Brennan's voice is low and absolute.
"Every human being — every single one — is worthy of respect simply because they exist. Not because of what they can do. Not because of what they can control."
He turns to face you fully.
"What happened to you does not diminish you. What they DID to you diminishes THEM."
He touches the cross at his collar.
"Remember that. On the bad days especially. You are still you."

Father Brennan adjusts his clerical collar — without the jacket, just his black shirt and white tab.
"Keep the jacket as long as you need. Return it to the chapel when you're done — or don't. I have others."
He checks the corridor.
"The nearest changing area is two doors down on the left. The orderly on that wing takes a break in twelve minutes."
Always watching. Always counting.
"God be with you. Though between you and me..."
He glances at the ward.
"...I think God has some explaining to do about this place."
He walks away, hands folded, every step measured and deliberate.

dialogue_tum_accident.text:
Father Brennan appears from nowhere — or perhaps he was always nearby, watching his flock.
He takes in the situation in an instant. Without a word, he steps between you and the corridor, his broad shoulders blocking the view of anyone passing by.
His jacket comes off. A blanket appears from somewhere — he must keep them stashed.
"I'm here. You're safe."
His voice is barely a whisper.
"You are still a person. Never forget that."

dialogue_tum_accident.text:
Father Brennan crouches beside you, keeping himself positioned as a wall between you and the world.
"Breathe. Just breathe."
His hand is on your shoulder — steady as bedrock.
"I know what you're feeling right now. Shame. Humiliation. A voice telling you this proves something about you."
His voice hardens.
"That voice is a LIE. This was done to you. Deliberately. By people who profit from your suffering."
He wraps the blanket around you.
"The only people who should feel shame right now are the ones with clipboards standing in the hallway writing notes instead of helping."

actions.label: How can you be so... unflinching?

dialogue_tum_accident.text:
"You don't have to explain. You don't have to apologize. You don't have to say anything at all."
Father Brennan adjusts the blanket.
"But if you want to talk, I'm listening. That's what I'm here for."
He sits on the floor beside you — directly on the hospital tile, black trousers and all. Not standing over you. BESIDE you.
"In thirty years of ministry, I've learned that the best thing a priest can do in a moment like this is shut up and sit down."
A beat.
"So. Here I am. Sitting."

actions.label: I hate this. I hate what I've become.

dialogue_tum_accident.text:
Father Brennan says nothing. He simply sits beside you on the cold hospital floor and lets you cry.
No shushing. No 'it's okay.' No platitudes. Just presence.
After a while — it could be a minute or ten — he speaks.
"I sat with a patient last week. Mr. Okafor. He was a structural engineer. Built bridges in three countries."
His voice is soft.
"He had an episode just like this. And afterward, he looked at me and said, 'Father, am I still a man?'"
Brennan's eyes are bright.
"I told him what I'm telling you: you are more than what your body does. You are more than what they've made you. You are a soul, and souls don't break."

"Hate this? Good. HATE it."
Father Brennan's voice is suddenly fierce.
"But hate the RIGHT thing. Don't hate yourself — hate the people who did this. Hate the corporation that profits from it. Hate the system that protects them."
He leans forward.
"Every ounce of shame you're feeling right now? That's not yours. It BELONGS to them. They manufactured it along with the compound."
His eyes burn.
"You didn't become anything. You were MADE into this, against your will, by people who see you as a revenue stream. Direct your fury where it belongs."
He stands and offers his hand.
"Now. Let's get you cleaned up before the orderlies arrive and write another note on their clipboards."

"Unflinching?"
Father Brennan almost laughs.
"I flinch plenty. I just do it later, in the chapel, alone, at two in the morning."
His mask slips — just for a second — and you see exhaustion and fury in equal measure.
"I've held the hands of people while they died. I've sat with parents burying children. But this—"
He gestures at the ward.
"This is worse. Because the suffering here was DESIGNED. Nobody dies. They just... diminish. And the people responsible call it healthcare."
He composes himself.
"So no, I don't flinch. Because if I start, I won't stop. And these patients need someone steady."

Father Brennan helps you to your feet with the brisk competence of a man who's done this many times.
"Supply closet, third door on the right. Fresh gowns, towels, the works. I stocked it yesterday."
He walks beside you, shielding you from view the entire way.
"I keep supplies in three locations across the hospital. The staff don't notice — they think housekeeping moves things around."
At the closet door, he stops.
"Take what you need. I'll stand out here."
He positions himself in the corridor like a sentry — arms folded, collar gleaming, the very picture of a chaplain waiting patiently.
But his eyes sweep the hallway, counting cameras, tracking orderlies.
Always watching over his flock.

When you emerge, Father Brennan nods once.
"Better."
He takes the soiled blanket without hesitation and folds it under his arm.
"I'll take care of this. Don't worry about it."
He pulls one last prayer card from his pocket — this one dog-eared and well-handled — and presses it into your hand.
"Psalm 34:18. 'The Lord is close to the brokenhearted and saves those who are crushed in spirit.'"
On the back, in his tiny handwriting: another guard schedule, another camera blind spot, another piece of the puzzle.
"I believe in redemption. Not for this hospital — for the people inside it."
He walks away, soiled blanket folded neatly under his arm, straight-backed, unhurried, unashamed.
A shepherd, tending his flock in a house of wolves.
